```ts
type GroupView = GroupHeader & { base_revision: number; origin?: { object: ObjectId; action: string };
                 undoes?: number; undone: boolean; names: Record<ObjectId, string>; effects?: EffectView[] };
type CellStateView = { kind: "literal"; value: WireValue } | { kind: "formula"; source?: string; override?: WireValue };
type LocationView = { type: "board"; board: BoardId } | { type: "container"; container: ObjectId | null; index: number };
type ObjectSnapshotView = { id: ObjectId; is_template: boolean; is_zone: boolean; is_character: boolean;
  tag?: string[]; shape?: Shape | null; contents?: (ObjectId | null)[];
  cells: Record<string, CellStateView>; cell_visibility?: Record<string, WireViewers>; actions: ActionView[] };
type EffectView =
  | { type: "cell"; object: ObjectId; cell: string; before: CellStateView | null; after: CellStateView | null; cause: "edit" | "roll" }
  | { type: "cell_visibility"; object: ObjectId; cell: string; before: WireViewers | null; after: WireViewers | null }
  | { type: "field"; object: ObjectId; field: "tag"; before: string[]; after: string[] }
  | { type: "field"; object: ObjectId; field: "shape"; before: Shape | null; after: Shape | null }
  | { type: "field"; object: ObjectId; field: "is_template" | "is_character"; before: boolean; after: boolean }
  | { type: "field"; object: ObjectId; field: "actions"; before: ActionView[]; after: ActionView[] }
  | { type: "place"; object: ObjectId; before: LocationView; after: LocationView }
  | { type: "create" | "remove"; location: LocationView; objects: ObjectSnapshotView[] }
  | { type: "reorder"; container: ObjectId; before: (ObjectId | null)[]; after: (ObjectId | null)[] }
  | { type: "board"; before: Board | null; after: Board | null }
  | { type: "allocate"; ids: ObjectId[]; seq_before: number; seq_after: number }
  | { type: "retire"; ids: ObjectId[] };
```

GM: the group's fields plus `undone`; effects converted losslessly (literal content → `{kind:"literal", value}`, formula → `{kind:"formula", source, override?}`, snapshots with every field, actions with `when` and `steps`). Character, by visibility at the view's revision (an object that does not exist then counts as invisible), per variant: `cell` kept iff the object is visible and the cell readable, no `source`, values redacted; `cell_visibility` dropped; `field` `tag`/`shape` kept iff that cell is readable, `is_template`/`is_character` iff the object is visible, `actions` iff the object is visible with names only; `place` kept iff the object is visible and its `board` and `container` cells readable, a container the viewer cannot see shown as `null`; `create`/`remove` kept iff at least one of its objects is visible, `objects` limited to the visible ones, each with only readable cells, no `source`, no `cell_visibility`, actions names only, `tag`/`shape`/`contents` omitted when unreadable and invisible contents ids as `null`, a hidden location container as `null`; `reorder` kept iff the container is visible and its `contents` readable, invisible ids as `null`; `board` always kept; `allocate`, `retire` dropped. `names[id]` present only when the viewer can see object `id` and read its `name` cell. `label`: kept only when every effect of the group other than `allocate`/`retire` is kept unreduced for the viewer (no effect dropped, no cell, object, value or id omitted, nulled or redacted); otherwise `null`, and clients show the group's `kind`. Commit-event headers go to connections (GM authority) and always carry the label. A character group view whose names and filtered effects are both empty is omitted (null); the decision is the same whether or not effects are requested. Otherwise its header is kept.

### §8 Subscriptions, commit events, ordering, reconnection

- Scopes at a revision: `board` = every object directly on the board and, recursively, their contents; `objects` = the ids (with `subtree`, also their descendants); `all` = every live object; `log` = no objects, the window of the newest `max_log_window` (200) retained groups. At most `max_subscriptions` per connection (`busy`). Subscription ids are opaque strings.
- `subscribe` returns full views and covers (§7.5); for `log`, `groups` = the window's group views newest first (character nulls omitted), `objects` and `covers` empty.
- Events:

```ts
{ type: "event"; event: "commit"; revision: number; group: GroupHeader; boards?: BoardView[]; deltas: SubscriptionDelta[] }
{ type: "event"; event: "save"; status: "saved" | "saved_not_durable" | "failed"; revision: number; message?: string }
type SubscriptionDelta = { subscription: string; objects: ObjectView[]; removed: ObjectId[];
  covers?: { upsert: Cover[]; removed: string[] }; groups_upserted?: GroupView[]; groups_removed?: number[] };
```

- One `commit` event per commit to every ready connection; `boards` (all boards) present when the group has any `board` effect; `deltas` holds one entry per subscription of that connection whose views changed (`[]` when none). `objects` = views whose content changed (whole views), `removed` = ids that left scope, were removed or became invisible; covers diffed by key; for `log`: `groups_upserted` = group views new to the window or changed (an undone group re-sent with `undone: true`; older groups whose filtered view changed after a reveal, hide or remove), `groups_removed` = indices that left the window or became omitted. Applying every delta to the initial result yields what a fresh `subscribe` at that revision returns. Board creation and removal (including undo) are visibility-relevant for character subscriptions: object views holding refs to that board (for example in viewers values) are rebuilt, and log-window group views holding refs to it are rebuilt (`redacted` while the board is gone, restored on undo).
- Evaluation (FORMULAS §7): after each commit the authority evaluates what the changed subscribed views need: their cells, those cells' transitive dependencies, and the visibility and geometry inputs the views and covers need, even outside the scope; every other dirty cell stays dirty until read.
- Ordering (D22): per connection, one message at a time in arrival order (the next waits for the previous response); all methods but `save` are synchronous; commit events are sent before the committing request's response; every connection sees commit events in revision order; a `save` response follows its `save` event.
- Heartbeat: ws ping every 15 s; two missed pongs terminate the connection.
- Reconnection (D23): no resumption. The client reconnects with backoff, sends `hello` with the same `client.instance`, resubscribes every live subscription with its original params (the subscription id may change), replaces its mirrors and reports a `resync` (`from_revision`, `to_revision`, `session_changed`). A resubscribe that fails for a transport reason (socket closed or timeout) keeps that subscription `recovering` (mirror kept, not updated) and it is resubscribed on the next connection; a resubscribe answered with an error response (e.g. `not_found` for a board removed meanwhile) makes it terminal: an `error` report with the server's `ProtocolError`, its mirror emptied, the subscription object (and an MCP handle) kept but no longer updated. The client becomes ready for ordinary callers only when every live subscription is resubscribed or terminal; until then `connectionError()` is `{code: "disconnected", recovering: true}`. Pending queries fail `disconnected`; writes per §6. Credentials are refreshed per §2. Every successful reconnect's `welcome.table.path` and `welcome.table.id` are compared with the identity captured at the first `welcome` before any subscription is rebound or any write is retried; a mismatch is `wrong_table`: terminal with explicit credentials; with discovery, the client re-reads the session file and retries once with its credentials, and a second mismatch is terminal.
- Mirror revision: on every processed commit event the client advances every live mirror's `revision` to the event's revision, also for subscriptions with no delta in it; after a processed commit a mirror's revision equals the client's revision.

### §9 Explain, evaluate, at_position, changes_since, document

```ts
type DepNode = { type: "cell"; object: ObjectId | null; cell: string; value?: WireResult; hidden?: true; dependencies?: DepNode[] }
             | { type: "exists"; object: ObjectId | null; exists?: boolean } | { type: "index" };
type ExplainCellResult = { revision: number; object: ObjectId; cell: string; view: CellView;
  content: { type: "literal" } | { type: "structural" } | { type: "formula"; source?: string; overridden: boolean; parses: boolean; syntax_error?: string };
  dependencies: DepNode[]; truncated: boolean;
  error_chain?: { object: ObjectId | null; cell: string | null; code: string }[];
  last_write?: GroupHeader & { cause: "edit" | "roll" } };
type ExplainGroupResult = { group: GroupView; action?: { object: ObjectId; name: string; when?: string; steps: string[]; current: true } };
type ExplainActionResult = { object: ObjectId; action: string; enabled: boolean; reason?: "when_false" | "when_error";
  guard?: { source?: string; value: WireResult }; steps?: string[] };   // guard present only when the action has a `when`
```

- `explain_cell`: the cell's value first (forcing evaluation), then its recorded dependencies breadth first to `depth`, each cell expanded once, at most `max_explain_nodes` nodes (`truncated` when cut); `error_chain` follows error origins to a self-originating error or a repeat, at most 32 steps; `last_write` = the header of the newest retained group with a `cell` effect on that cell, as the viewer would see it in the log (§7.6: for a character, `label` is `null` unless every effect is visible unreduced; omitted when that group's view is omitted for the viewer). Character viewer: a dependency cell it cannot see is `{type:"cell", object, cell, hidden: true}` without value; a dependency on an object it cannot see has `object: null` and no value; no `source`; values redacted; error-chain entries on invisible objects or cells have `object: null` or `cell: null`.
- `explain_group`: the group view with effects (§7.6) and, for the GM when the origin object still exists, the origin action's current definition (`current: true`).
- `explain_action`: `enabled` (top level) is true iff the action has no `when` or its `when`, evaluated with `this` = the object, is `true`; `reason` (top level, only when not enabled) is `when_false` (any non-error non-true value) or `when_error`; `guard` is present only when there is a `when`, with its `value` and, for the GM, its `source`; `steps` GM only. An action without `when` gives `{enabled: true}` with no `reason` and no `guard`, for every viewer.
- Not found: a nonexistent object, cell, action or group, and one the viewer cannot see (invisible object, unreadable cell, omitted group), answer the identical error `{code:"not_found", message:"not found"}`.
- `evaluate` (D28): GM only; `source.length` > `max_source_length` is `bad_request`; unknown `this` is `not_found`; without `this` the engine's ad hoc default.
- `at_position` (D29): candidates from the spatial index at the point; `objects` = non-zone objects directly on the board whose evaluated footprint contains the point (boundary inclusive; shapeless within epsilon), ascending `z` (empty = 0) then id; `zones` likewise; both filtered by the viewer's visibility. A candidate whose evaluated `position`, `rotation`, `shape` or `z` is an error (including `#LIMIT` from an exhausted budget) has no geometry and is omitted, as the spatial index treats non-finite bounds; the request never fails for this reason.
- `changes_since`: scans retained groups with `revision > params.revision`, oldest first, at most `limit` scanned; returns the non-omitted group views among them with effects; `more` = retained groups remain after the last scanned; `next_revision` = the `revision` of the last scanned group (its `base_revision` + 1), or the current revision when none was scanned; passing `next_revision` back as `revision` continues after the scanned groups, so pages of only invisible groups still advance. `truncated` = `params.revision` < `floor` (§6; with no retained groups the floor is the current revision); `params.revision` above the current revision is `bad_request`.
- `document` (D30): GM only; canonical `Snapshot` and retained log, unfiltered.

### §10 Errors, rejections, limits

```ts
type ProtocolError = { code: ProtocolErrorCode; message: string; details?: unknown };
type ProtocolErrorCode = "bad_request" | "unknown_method" | "unauthorized" | "protocol_version" | "busy"
  | "too_large" | "not_found" | "unsupported" | "internal" | "disconnected" | "timeout" | "uncertain" | "wrong_table"
  | "retry_unknown";
type Rejection =   // @vtt/schema, complete
  | { type: "protected_cell"; object: ObjectId; cell: string }
  | { type: "containment_cycle"; object: ObjectId; container: ObjectId }
  | { type: "undo_conflict"; target: number; conflicting: number[]; message: string }
  | { type: "nothing_to_undo" }
  | { type: "type_error"; object: ObjectId; cell: string; expected: string }
  | { type: "invalid"; message: string };
type ProtocolRejection = Rejection
  | { type: "stale_write"; base_revision: number; revision: number; floor: number; truncated: boolean;
      conflicts: { index: number; revision: number; actor: Actor; label: string; keys: string[] }[] }
  | { type: "undo_target_changed"; expected: number; actual: number | null };
type Limits = { max_message_bytes: 1048576; max_ops: 1000; max_page: 200; max_ids: 200; max_subscriptions: 16;
  max_explain_depth: 4; max_explain_nodes: 200; max_source_length: 10000; max_groups: 500; max_log_window: 200;
  max_txn_ids_per_client: 1000; max_requests_per_second: 200; max_buffered_bytes: 67108864 };
```

- Errors are protocol failures (the request was not processed as a command); rejections are command outcomes (`status: "rejected"`). `disconnected` (only for requests never written to a socket), `timeout` (queries only; a timed-out write is `uncertain`), `uncertain` and `wrong_table` are produced by the client library only; `retry_unknown` is produced by the authority (§6) and mapped to `uncertain` by the client. A response whose `result` fails the schema of the pending request's method rejects that request on the client with `{code: "internal", message, details: {type: "protocol", method}}`; the connection stays open and no mirror changes. An unparseable request answers `bad_request` and the connection stays open; any unexpected server exception answers `internal` and the connection stays open.
- `max_message_bytes` applies to client-to-server frames only (a larger frame closes the connection); server-to-client messages have no size limit. More than `max_requests_per_second` requests per connection answer `busy` (token bucket). A connection whose unsent buffer exceeds `max_buffered_bytes` is closed 4429.

### §11 MCP

Tools (17):

| Tool | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| table_info | `{revision, boards, table /* {name, path, id} */, limits, actor, session}` from the client |
| list_objects, get_objects, evaluate, zones, at_position, changes_since, log | the same-named methods |
| explain_cell, explain_group, explain_action | the same-named methods |
| transact | `transact` with `base_revision` required; `txn_id` always generated by the MCP server; a lost response is retried per §6 within 10 s; `uncertain` is reported as an error |
| undo | `undo` (targets `latest`, `mine`, `group`; `expect_index`) |
| save | `save` |
| subscribe | `subscribe` (scopes `board`, `objects`, `all`; GM viewer); returns `{subscription: <handle>, revision, objects: <count>}` |
| poll_changes | `{subscription: <handle>, wait_ms?: 0..30000 (default 0)}` → `{subscription, revision, changes: ChangeRecord[], overflowed: boolean}`; returns and clears the buffer, waiting up to `wait_ms` for the first record |
| unsubscribe | `unsubscribe`, drops the buffer and the handle |

- Input schemas: explicit MCP schemas derived from the protocol params schemas, strict (unknown keys are an MCP input error), with transport-managed fields removed (`transact`: no `actor`, `retry`, `txn_id`) and variants narrowed (`undo` target: `latest`, `mine`, `group`); an input that fails them reaches no handler and sends nothing to the authority. Results are `structuredContent` plus one JSON text block. A `ProtocolError` → `isError: true` with `{code, message}`; `status: "rejected"` → `isError: true` with the rejection and `op_index`.
- Handles: `"m"` + a counter, owned by the MCP process; a handle stays valid across reconnects while the protocol subscription id behind it changes.
- Connection gate: while the client reports a connection error (`disconnected`, including `recovering: true` and the time before the first `welcome`, `unauthorized` or `wrong_table`), every tool, including `table_info` and `poll_changes`, returns `isError: true` with that error instead of its normal result.

```ts
type ChangeRecord =
  | { type: "commit"; revision: number; group: GroupHeader; created: ObjectId[]; removed: ObjectId[];
      cells: { object: ObjectId; cell: string; before?: CellView; after?: CellView }[];
      objects: { object: ObjectId; before?: ObjectFacts; after?: ObjectFacts }[] }
  | { type: "resync"; from_revision: number; to_revision: number; session_changed: boolean }
  | { type: "failed"; code: ProtocolErrorCode; message: string };   // the subscription became terminal (§8)
type ObjectFacts = { is_template: boolean; is_character: boolean; actions: ActionView[] };
```

- Per subscription a buffer of at most 1,000 records; beyond that the oldest is dropped and the next `poll_changes` result has `overflowed: true` (then reset). `objects` lists every object whose flags or actions differ between before and after. Each buffered record sends `notifications/resources/updated` for `vtt://subscriptions/<handle>`; reading that resource returns `{subscription, revision, overflowed, failed: {code, message} | null, objects: ObjectView[] /* current mirror */, changes: ChangeRecord[]}` without clearing, so an agent recovers current state after overflow by reading it. The `revision` of `poll_changes` results and of the resource is the mirror's revision (§8), which equals the client's current revision after a processed commit. A failed subscription's handle stays valid until `unsubscribe`; its polls return the buffered records (ending with the `failed` record) and then empty results.
- Resources: `vtt://docs/formulas`, `vtt://docs/design`, `vtt://docs/protocol` (the docs' text), `vtt://schema/ops` (JSON Schema of `WireOp`, 19 kinds), `vtt://subscriptions/<handle>`.
- Tool descriptions say: ids should be human-meaningful (DESIGN §5.3); writes need the latest `revision`; one `transact` is one undoable group; formulas and actions follow docs/FORMULAS.md.
- `vtt-mcp [--url u] [--token t] [--name n]`, else `VTT_URL`/`VTT_TOKEN`, else the session file (discovery mode, selected whenever no explicit credentials are given, even when the file is missing: the process stays up and connects once the file appears; credentials refreshed per §2 on every reconnect attempt, `wrong_table` stops it; startup fails only for malformed or incomplete explicit credentials); `kind: "agent"`; startup order: MCP initialization first, then `agent_name` = `--name`, else the MCP client's name, else `agent`, then the authority connection with recovery from the start, without requiring an initial successful connection (tools answer `disconnected` until the first `welcome`); stdio; logs to stderr only; while the authority is unreachable tools return `isError` `disconnected` and the client keeps reconnecting.

### §12 Additive extension

Protocol v1 grows only additively: new optional fields, new methods, new ops, new event kinds. M5 adds `invoke` behaviour, its MCP tool, and face-layout fields on views this way; a change that breaks a v1 client bumps `protocol`.

Compatibility policy (D32): the authority parses client messages strictly (unknown keys anywhere → `bad_request`; `__proto__` always rejected). Clients parse server messages forward-compatibly: unknown keys in any object are ignored (stripped), a message of unknown `type` or an event of unknown `event` kind is ignored with a warning, an unknown `EffectView` variant inside a group view is dropped with a warning; none of these closes the connection. `parseServerMessage` validates only the envelope (`welcome`, `response` with `id` and either `result` or `error`, `event`, `goodbye`); the client validates and normalizes a response's `result` against the result schema of the pending request's method, found by `id` (the wire carries no method on responses); unknown keys inside results, views and effects are stripped at that stage, not by envelope parsing. An envelope that is malformed in a known shape (missing or mistyped required fields) is still invalid; a result that fails its method's schema fails only that request (§10). Because clients ignore unknown keys, a new field must never change the meaning of existing fields; such a change bumps `protocol`.

## Doc edits

- docs/PROTOCOL.md (new): §1–§12 exactly as the contract above (D3–D30 cross-referenced).
- DESIGN.md §5.2: D1, the tool groups, D7, D21 and the view-as note of D4.
- DESIGN.md §7: Platform paragraph (D1, D2); Revisions (D7, D8); Persistence (D24, D25); a short **Protocol** paragraph pointing to PROTOCOL.md.
- DESIGN.md §4.4: D12, D14, D15, D16 (filtering of query results, explain and the log).
- FORMULAS.md §7 Propagation: "After each commit the authority recomputes what the changed subscribed views need (their cells, those cells' dependencies, and the visibility and geometry inputs of those views) and sends the views that changed; every other dirty cell stays dirty until read."
- CLAUDE.md: `protocol` in the package list (D2); the dependency line (D27).

Done when: every edit above is present; PROTOCOL.md contains every type, table, value and rule of the contract above with the same names (17 methods, 19 ops with their declared keys, 14 error codes, 13 limits, 5 close codes, the `EffectView` variants and their character filtering, the processing order of §6, the `changes_since` cursor, the log window, the credential-refresh, subscription-failure and mirror-revision rules, the lock protocol, the compatibility policy, and the complete `Rejection` union); DESIGN §10 has one row per decision D1–D33 except D13, D20 and D31; no code changes; `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm lint` exit 0.

Out of scope: any code; the M2 docs; vtt-75c.18's two rows; face layouts and action syntax (M5); asset naming and appearance cells (M4); chunked snapshot delivery (vtt-y1w.12) and persistent deduplication (vtt-y1w.11).

Depends on: none.

title: Authority: atomic save/load I/O and epic acceptance
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence ("Saves are atomic"; assets beside the file), §8.4 steps 6 and 15, with the save-failure and asset rules written by vtt-75c.2; the epic M2 done-when ("a document round-trips through the file format and undo of an op group is refused correctly after a conflicting op").

Filesystem I/O on top of vtt-75c.11's pure serialization, plus the epic acceptance test. Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/persist/io.ts (one added export line in src/persist/index.ts), test/epic-m2.test.ts, test/persist/io.test.ts.

- `saveTable(path, store, assets, fs = nodeFs)`: `serializeTable`, then writes `<path>.tmp-<pid>-<random>` in the same directory, fsyncs it, renames over `path`, then fsyncs the directory (ignoring `EISDIR`/`EPERM` on platforms that refuse directory fsync). Two failure stages: a failure before the rename (write, file fsync, rename) removes the temp file, leaves the original byte-identical, and returns `{ok: false, stage: "before_replace", error}`; a failure of the directory fsync after the rename leaves the new file in place and intact and returns `{ok: false, stage: "after_replace", error}` ("saved, durability not confirmed"). Success returns `{ok: true}`. `fs` is injectable for fault tests. Capture contract (needed by vtt-5su.4's save ordering): `saveTable` serializes the store and assets synchronously, before its first `await` (or any other suspension), so the bytes it writes are the state at the moment of the call; later mutations in the same tick do not reach the file.
- `loadTable(path, fs = nodeFs)`: reads the file and calls `parseTable`; then checks each asset path, resolved against the file's directory, for existence through `fs`; missing assets are warnings in the result, not errors.

test/epic-m2.test.ts: build a document with a board, a goblin and a spawned card holding a zone; apply a set, an override, a move, a spawn, a remove and an undo; save to a temp directory; load; `toSnapshot()` and the log (indices, `first_index`, barrier) deep-equal the originals; then on the loaded store the GM writes a cell, the agent writes the same cell, and `undo({type:"actor", actor: gm})` is refused with `undo_conflict`, while `undo({type:"latest"})` succeeds.

Done when: the epic test passes; save → load → save produces a byte-identical file; a fault-injected failure of the temp write, the temp fsync, and the rename each leave the original byte-identical, no temp file, and `stage: "before_replace"`; a fault-injected directory fsync failure leaves the new file intact (it loads) and returns `stage: "after_replace"`; `loadTable` warns about a missing asset and loads the document anyway; a test calls `saveTable` without awaiting, mutates the store in the same tick (a committed `writeValue`), then awaits the save and loads the file: it holds the pre-mutation state; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); serialization, parsing, migration, history validation, compaction (vtt-75c.11); autosave cadence and file location (M3); copying or importing asset files (M4).

Depends on: vtt-75c.11.

title: Authority: document store, transactions, replay
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 (document plus ordered op stream, transactions, commit point, internal synchronization before notifications, error handling, change summary, replay and rewind), as written by vtt-75c.2; FORMULAS.md §8.1 (atomicity); FIXTURES.md §8 (one group per committed step).

The transactional store over vtt-75c.5's `DocState`, effects, summary and `History`. Exclusive files in packages/authority/src/store/: document-store.ts, transaction.ts, replay.ts, compare.ts (export lines added to src/store/index.ts without reordering others).

- document-store.ts: `DocumentStore.fromSnapshot(snapshot, history?)` (validated with `validateSnapshot`), `toSnapshot()` (deep copy, canonical order: objects by id, cells and `cell_visibility` by name), the `DocState` read API, `revision`, `history`.
- transaction.ts: `store.begin(actor, {kind, label, origin?, undoes?})` returns a `Transaction`; one transaction at a time (`begin` while one is open throws). `tx.record(effect)` applies the effect to a working copy and appends it; `tx.doc` is the working copy's read API; `tx.changes()` is the live `ChangeSummary` so far. `commit()`: validates the working document with `validateSnapshot` (failure → `Rejected({type:"invalid"})`, nothing published); captures `names` (working-copy names for touched objects; for removed objects, the name just before removal); builds the `OpGroup` (`base_revision`, `revision = base_revision + 1`, `undoes`); then the commit point: the new document and the appended group are published atomically. Immediately after the commit point, internal synchronization hooks (`store.onCommitInternal(fn)`, run in registration order; used by the engine adapter and the index) run, then public `store.onCommit` listeners. Both receive the payload `{group, summary: ChangeSummary, before: DocState (read-only view of the pre-commit document)}`. An error thrown by a public listener is collected and reported (`commit()` returns `{group, summary, listenerErrors}`) and never undoes or aborts the commit; an error in an internal hook is a bug and propagates after the commit is published. `abort()` discards everything. A refusing primitive throws `Rejected` (carries a `Rejection`).
- `store.transact(actor, meta, fn)`: runs `fn(tx)`; a `Rejected` thrown before the commit point aborts and returns `{ok: false, rejection}`; any other error thrown before the commit point aborts and is rethrown unchanged (scenario errors stay scenario errors); success returns `{ok: true, group, summary, listenerErrors}`. An `onAbort` hook lets callers (the dice wrapper in vtt-75c.15) reset state on either pre-commit failure. A committed group with no effects is still a group.
- replay.ts: `replay(base, groups)`: applies each group's effects in order and sets `revision` to each group's `revision` (also for no-effect groups); requires `base.revision === groups[0].base_revision`. `rewind(head, groups)`: applies `applyHistoricalInverse` of each effect, groups and effects in reverse order, setting `revision` to each group's `base_revision`. Neither touches dice or evaluation.
- compare.ts: `storedStateEqual(a, b, {ignoreRevision = true, ignoreIdentity = false})` and `diffStoredState` (for messages): compare canonical snapshots, excluding `revision` by default and, with `ignoreIdentity`, `next_seq` and `retired_ids`. Shared by vtt-75c.8, vtt-75c.11 and the runner's `replay` expectation (vtt-75c.13).

Done when: tests (test/store/document-store.test.ts, transaction.test.ts, replay.test.ts, compare.test.ts) show: `fromSnapshot`/`toSnapshot` round-trip; `begin` while a transaction is open throws; a transaction whose working document fails validation on commit leaves no trace (document, history, revision); one committed transaction appends exactly one group with the next absolute index and increments `revision` by one; group `names` hold the name at commit time even after a later rename, and a removed object's name; the commit payload's summary matches the effects (spawn, same-value write, move with derived keys, remove) and `before` shows the pre-commit state; internal hooks run before public listeners, including a public listener registered before the internal hook was added; a throwing public listener does not abort the commit and is reported in `listenerErrors`; `transact` returns a rejection for `Rejected`, rethrows a `ScenarioError`-like custom error unchanged after aborting, and calls `onAbort` in both cases but not after a commit whose listener throws; `replay` from a base snapshot at revision 7 through groups including a no-effect group reproduces the head including `revision`, and `rewind` reproduces the base including `revision`, `next_seq` and `retired_ids`; `storedStateEqual` ignores `revision` by default and identity only when asked; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); effects, summary, history (vtt-75c.5); edit and structural primitives (vtt-75c.14, vtt-75c.6); undo selection (vtt-75c.8); persistence (vtt-75c.11, vtt-75c.17); formula evaluation (vtt-75c.12).

Depends on: vtt-75c.5.


Note from vtt-75c.5 as merged: `historicalInverse(effect, stateBefore)` takes the state before the effect (the inverse of a board removal records the board's index), so inverses cannot be derived while rewinding backward from a later state. The store computes each group's historical inverses while applying or replaying forward and keeps them in memory (never persisted), or rewinds by replaying from a snapshot. `History` returns deep-frozen records (`FrozenGroup`, `DeepReadonly<TableLog>`); copy before mutating.

API deviations accepted: rewind(head, groups, inverses) with replayWithInverses and store.inverses(index); onAbort passed as a fourth transact argument; begin validates kind/undoes pairing; O(n) deep copy per begin (copy-on-write is a possible Polish item, not filed).

title: Formula: engine integration (budget, spatial callbacks, ad hoc evaluation, exception recovery)
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §7 (query dependencies, budget, host-independence), §6 (spatial functions in the engine), §8.1 (`when` as an ordinary formula), §2.3 (#LIMIT), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §7 (budgets, responsiveness).

Complete the engine on top of vtt-o9i.9's core. Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/engine/env.ts (the recording `EvalEnv`'s query methods), budget.ts, adhoc.ts (export lines added to src/index.ts without reordering). Tests test/engine-integration-*.test.ts with `MemoryHost` (vtt-o9i.15) and the queries of vtt-o9i.8.

- Query methods. The engine's `EvalEnv` implements `objectsOnBoard(board, near)` by calling `host.objectsOnBoard(board, near)` (the host never evaluates; the candidate set is defined over literal geometry) and records an `{index}` dependency; `allObjects` and `objectsNamed` likewise record `{index}`. Geometry of candidates is read by the evaluator through the ordinary recording `read`, so formula positions are cell dependencies and can close a cycle (vtt-o9i.9's cycle rules apply).
- Budget. Each formula evaluation (final attempt) may spend `options.budget` (default 20,000): each cell read, each existence check, each candidate tested by a spatial query, and each id returned by `allObjects`/`objectsNamed` costs 1; reading an already computed dependency costs 1 regardless of its own cost. Because the candidate set is host-independent, the charge is the same on every host. Exceeding the budget gives #LIMIT (origin itself); dependents see the propagated error. Results never depend on cache state or read order.
- Ad hoc. `engine.evaluate(source, {thisId})` parses and evaluates with the same recording env (reads use and populate the memo) but keeps no dependency entry for itself; it is how `when` guards and show-when are evaluated.
- Host exceptions propagate out of `value`/`evaluate`; the engine first resets every in-progress cell (and the work stack) to dirty, so the engine stays usable.

Done when: tests show: a zone's `contents(this)` cell recomputes after `MemoryHost.move` brings an object it never returned into the zone, and after `createObject` places one inside; `obj("Goblin")` changes after a `set` of the goblin's `name`; a cycle through a spatial query (a token whose formula `position` depends on the `contents(...)` of a zone it is a candidate of) is #CYCLE and recovers after `replaceContent`; `objects(…)` over 30 objects with `budget: 50` is #LIMIT while a sibling cell is fine; budget-limited results are identical cold, warm and in reversed read order; host equivalence: with a deliberately small budget, the same formulas give identical results and identical #LIMIT outcomes on `MemoryHost` (brute force) and on a test-only grid-indexed host computing the same literal-geometry candidate set, including objects with formula positions, a candidate whose position formula is an error, and a cycle through geometry; `engine.evaluate("hit and dmg = empty", {thisId})` for the attack card's guards; a host that throws mid-evaluation leaves the engine usable and the next read correct; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); the core resolution, memo, graph and cycles (vtt-o9i.9); query semantics (vtt-o9i.8); finer index keys (Polish); action reads (vtt-75c.15).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.9, vtt-o9i.8, vtt-o9i.12.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Codex review (.reviews/vtt-o9i.16-* on the branch): no findings. Budget costs as implemented: 1 per read (any cell), 1 per existence check (incl. validateRefs checks on literals), 1 per distinct candidate id from objectsOnBoard, 1 per id from allObjects/objectsNamed; charged per attempt, only the final attempt decides. Core edits limited to wiring (ResolveContext.budget, PENDING exported, env moved to env.ts, withBudget around the evaluator, Engine.evaluate). Exception recovery needed no reset code (results stored only when a component completes). GridHost test host under test/support/grid-host.ts.

title: Formula: MemoryHost (mutable test document, landing rules, change reporting)
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3.1 (structural defaults, landing rule, literal-only `name` and `tag`), §6 (the literal-geometry candidate set), as written by vtt-o9i.12 and vtt-75c.2; docs/FIXTURES.md §3 (setup), §6 (`move` destinations).

`MemoryHost`: the mutable test document every engine, runner and acceptance test in M1 uses. Exclusive file: packages/formula/test/support/memory-host.ts. It implements vtt-o9i.3's `EvalHost`.

- `MemoryHost.fromSetup(setup)`: cells from `cells` (literals as-is, `{type:"formula"}` as formula content); structural cells derived as FIXTURES §3 says (`id`, `tag`, `contents`, derived `container`, `board` and `position` from `placement`, `shape` as a ShapeValue, `is_zone`), every other §3.1 cell defaulted per vtt-o9i.3's table; a formula in `name` or `tag` is a setup error (thrown); ids in `setup.characters` get `is_character`. Boards `exists()` and have no cells.
- `objectsOnBoard(board, near)`: the candidate set by brute force over literal geometry, exactly as vtt-o9i.3's contract defines it: objects directly on the board whose literal `indexBounds` (vtt-75c.7) intersect `near` (`boundsIntersect`), plus every object on the board with a formula-valued `position`, `rotation`, `z` or `shape` (no override). Never evaluates formulas. Also exported as `literalCandidates(host, board, near)`, the reference other hosts are tested against.
- Test-only mutators, each returning the `Change[]` to feed `engine.invalidate`, covering every cell whose content changed, including derived `container` and both containers' `contents`:
  - `set(id, cell, value)` (creates an absent cell); `override(id, cell, value)`; `clearOverride(id, cell)`; `replaceContent(id, cell, content)` (literal or formula; drops any override; a formula on `name` or `tag` throws).
  - `move(id, dest)`, `dest` a FIXTURES §6 board destination `{board, position}` or container destination `{container, index}`, with the landing rules of FORMULAS §3.1: leaves its old container's `contents` or board; container destination inserts at `index` (default append) and deletes `position`, `rotation`, `z`; board destination sets `board`, empties `container`, writes `position` as a literal (as an override if it holds a formula), sets `z` to 1 + the maximum literal `z` of the other objects on that board (absent or empty as 0) unless `z` holds a formula, keeps `rotation` on board-to-board moves; `owner` never changes.
  - `createObject(id, init)`: `init` = `{cells?, tag?, shape?, is_zone?, placement: {board, position} | {container, index?}}`; returns `object_created` plus the parent's `contents` change when placed in a container.
  - `deleteObject(id)`: recursive over `contents`; returns `object_deleted` for every removed object plus the surviving parent's `contents` change.
  - `isOverridden(id, cell)`.

Done when: test/memory-host.test.ts: `fromSetup` over every scenario builds without error; hit-points.json `cell("aldric","hp")` is the formula content and `cell("aldric","max_hp")` is `num(27)`; dice-tray.json `cell("cup","contents")` is an empty list, `cell("tray","is_zone")` is `true`, `cell("tray","shape")` is the rect ShapeValue; fireball.json `cell("fireball_zone","container")` is `ref("fireball")` and `cell("fireball_zone","board")` is empty; unset `face_up` reads `true`, unset `visible_to` viewers ["all"], unset `z` empty; a setup with a formula `name` throws; `objectsOnBoard` returns objects whose literal bounds meet the box, an offset polygon whose anchor is in the box while its footprint is not, an object with a formula `position` far outside the box, and nothing inside a container or on another board; an object whose formula `position` has an override is a candidate only by its literal bounds; each mutator returns the right `Change`s: set / override / clearOverride / replaceContent (literal → formula, formula → literal, override dropped), move into a container (deletes `position`, `rotation`, `z`, updates both `contents`), move onto a board (lands one above the highest literal `z`), createObject on a board and in a container, deleteObject of an object holding two others (three `object_deleted` plus the parent's `contents`); `isOverridden` tracks overrides; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); host types, `FakeEnv`, fixture conversion (vtt-o9i.3); exact spatial tests (vtt-o9i.8); the engine (vtt-o9i.9); spawn, undo, bindings (M2, M5).

title: Authority: action context and dice sources
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §8.1 ("Reads inside an action"), §2.2 and §8.3 (`roll`, `shuffle` as the only randomness), as written by vtt-75c.2; FIXTURES.md §5 (the dice script: order, normalized `expr` match, permutation, atomicity, exhaustion and leftover as scenario errors).

Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/engine/action-context.ts, dice.ts (export lines added to src/engine/index.ts without reordering others).

action-context.ts, `ActionContext(table, tx)` for M5: implements vtt-o9i.3's `EvalEnv` over a committed `Table` and an open transaction (vtt-75c.16), using the transaction's live change summary `tx.changes()` and working copy `tx.doc`. Reads, in this order:

1. Transaction-local existence: an object removed earlier in `tx` does not exist (`exists` false; any read of it is #REF, even if it was written before its removal); an object that neither exists at the start of the action nor was created in `tx` does not exist.
2. An object created in `tx` (spawned or created): its cells read from the working copy: a literal reads as the literal; a cell with an override reads as the override (copied overrides included); structural cells read from the working copy with structural defaults; a formula cell without override reads `empty` (formulas are not evaluated before commit).
3. An existing object: a cell whose stored state was changed in `tx` (as listed in `tx.changes()`: written cells, including same-value writes, and move-derived cells) reads from the working copy: a literal or override as written; structural and move-derived cells (`board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container`, `contents`, `tag`, `shape`) as they now stand; a cell whose content was replaced by a formula in `tx` reads `empty`.
4. Any other cell reads as of the start of the action: `table.value` (still the pre-action value, because recompute runs only after commit).

Query and existence methods complete the `EvalEnv` contract against the working copy: `exists` by rule 1 (created and removed objects from `tx.changes()`); `objectsNamed` and `allObjects` over working-copy objects (literal names); `objectsOnBoard(board, near)` returns the literal-geometry candidate set (FORMULAS §6) computed by brute force over the working copy's literal geometry, never evaluating formulas (an index reflects only committed state); candidate geometry is then read by the evaluator through this context's reads, so the candidate set and budget equal what any host would give for that state.

dice.ts: `DiceSource { roll(dice): RollValue; permutation(n): number[]; mark(): number; reset(mark): void }`.
- `RandomDiceSource(seed)`: a seedable PRNG implemented in this file (a small, documented generator such as sfc32 or xoshiro128**) whose whole state is copyable; `mark()` returns a copy of the state and `reset(mark)` restores it, so after a reset the source behaves exactly as if the aborted draws never happened, whatever ranges are requested next. Range mapping is unbiased (rejection sampling). Rolling uses vtt-o9i.13's `rollDice` through a `RandomSource` adapter; permutations use Fisher–Yates on the same generator.
- `ScriptedDiceSource(entries)`: hands out FIXTURES §5 entries in order, throwing `ScenarioError` on exhaustion, kind mismatch, or an `expr` not equal to the requested dice by vtt-o9i.5's `diceEquals`; `mark`/`reset` move its position; `remaining()`.
- `rollInto(tx, source, obj, cell, dice)` = `source.roll` then vtt-75c.14's `rollWrite(tx, …)`; `shuffleWith(tx, source, container)` = `source.permutation(len)` then `reorder(tx, …)`.
- `transactWithDice(table, actor, meta, source, fn)` (exported from this file, so table.ts is not edited): marks the source, then runs `store.transact` with an `onAbort` that resets it. A `Rejected` before the commit point returns the rejection; any other error before the commit point (including `ScenarioError` from a scripted source) aborts, resets the source, and propagates unchanged; after the commit point the source is never reset, even if a public listener throws. So a refused or aborted transaction consumes no randomness and no script entries.

Done when: tests show: `ActionContext` reads written values; start-of-action values for unwritten formula cells even after a write to their input; `empty` for a formula cell on an object spawned in the same transaction; a copied literal and a copied override on a spawned object read as copied; after a move in `tx`, the moved object's `position`, `board`, `container` and both containers' `contents` read as moved; write → remove → read of the same object gives #REF; `exists` of a removed and of a created object; `objectsOnBoard` includes a spawned object and excludes a removed one; the scripted source matches `1d8+3` against a request equal by normalization, throws on mismatch and exhaustion, and is reset after an aborted transaction; `RandomDiceSource`: an aborted transaction containing a `1d20` roll and a shuffle of 5, followed by a `3d6` roll, a `1d100` roll and a shuffle of 3, yields exactly the same results as a control run that performs only the latter three; a refused transaction behaves the same; a `ScenarioError` thrown inside `transactWithDice` propagates unchanged and the scripted source is reset; a committed transaction whose public listener throws keeps its consumed entries; seeded runs are deterministic; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); the action runner (`when`, steps, `each`, step errors: M5); the host adapter and recompute (vtt-75c.12); cryptographic randomness.

Depends on: vtt-75c.12, vtt-o9i.13.

title: Authority: cell, field, reorder and board edit primitives
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1 (cells), §4.2 (literals, formulas, overrides), §4.4 (per-cell visibility metadata); FORMULAS.md §3.1 (protected cells; literal-only `name` and `tag`; edit-only `shape`), §8.2 ("Writing to a cell that holds a formula creates an override… Writing to a protected cell is an error"), as written by vtt-75c.2 and vtt-o9i.12; FIXTURES.md §6 (`set`, `override`, `clear_override` meanings).

The edit primitives over vtt-75c.16's transactions. Each primitive is a function taking the open `Transaction` as its first argument and recording effects through `tx.record`, so no bead edits transaction.ts after vtt-75c.16. Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/store/edits.ts (re-exported through one added line in src/store/index.ts). Tests: test/store/edits.test.ts.

- `writeValue(tx, obj, cell, value)`: literal or absent cell becomes that literal; a formula cell gets `override = value`. Absent cells are created (FIXTURES §6 `set`).
- `setFormula(tx, obj, cell, source)`: replaces content with a formula, dropping any override.
- `clearOverride(tx, obj, cell)`: removes the override; `invalid` if none.
- `deleteCell(tx, obj, cell)`; `renameCell(tx, obj, from, to)`: refuses with `protected_cell` if `from` or `to` is any FORMULAS §3.1 structural name; refuses with `invalid` if `from` is absent or `to` exists; otherwise deletes and creates in one group (formulas naming the old name are not rewritten); per-cell visibility: any `cell_visibility` entry already recorded for the absent `to` is replaced by `from`'s entry, or removed if `from` has none, and `from`'s entry is removed.
- `setCellVisibility(tx, obj, cell, viewers | null)`: writes the per-object `cell_visibility` metadata (`cell_visibility` effect); valid for any cell name, including structural, field-backed, derived, and absent cells; `viewers` must be a non-empty literal viewers value (else `type_error`).
- `rollWrite(tx, obj, cell, roll)`: as `writeValue` with `cause: "roll"`.
- `setTag(tx, obj, tags)`, `setShape(tx, obj, shape | null)`, `setTemplateFlag(tx, obj, bool)`, `setCharacterFlag(tx, obj, bool)` (`field` effects).
- `reorder(tx, container, permutation)`: `new[i] = old[permutation[i]]` (FIXTURES §5); `invalid` unless a permutation of the length.
- `addBoard(tx, id, name?)`: `id` must satisfy `isValidId` and not be reserved (a live board, a live object, or retired; else `invalid`); records an `allocate` effect for the id (no `next_seq` change) and a `board` creation effect. `renameBoard(tx, id, name)` (`board` effect).

Protection and types: writing `id`, `board`, `is_zone`, `contents`, `container` through any cell primitive throws `protected_cell`; writing `shape` through `writeValue`, `setFormula` or `rollWrite` throws `protected_cell` (only `setShape` changes it); `template` and `name` accept literals only (`setFormula` on them is `type_error`); `tag` through `writeValue` must be a list of text and becomes a `setTag`, and `setFormula` on `tag` is `type_error`; `position` may be written only on a board object (else `protected_cell`); `opaque` only on zones; literal structural writes are type-checked against `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` (`type_error`). Deleting a structural cell is `protected_cell`.

Done when: tests show each primitive's effects and resulting state; `writeValue` on a formula cell creates an override and `clearOverride` restores formula tracking at the stored level; `clearOverride` without override is `invalid`; every protected write (including `writeValue` on `shape`) throws `protected_cell` and leaves the document and history unchanged; `setFormula` on `name`, `tag`, `template` is `type_error`; `setShape` changes the shape with a `field` effect; `setCellVisibility` on `contents` and on `tag` of an object with no such stored cells records a `cell_visibility` effect, and clearing it with `null` removes the entry; `renameCell` moves the visibility entry; `renameCell` to `container`, to `shape`, and from `name` are `protected_cell`; `renameCell` onto an existing cell is `invalid`; `renameCell` onto an absent cell that has its own `cell_visibility` entry replaces that entry with the source's (and removes it when the source has none); `addBoard` with an id used by a live object, by a live board, or retired is `invalid`, and a valid `addBoard` records `allocate` plus `board`; `reorder` with `[2,0,1]` on `[a,b,c]` gives `[c,a,b]`; a rename of `name` is captured in the next group's `names`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); effects, history (vtt-75c.5); store and transactions (vtt-75c.16); move, create, spawn, remove (vtt-75c.6); undo (vtt-75c.8); evaluation and dice sources (vtt-75c.12, vtt-75c.15); `add` as an arithmetic step (M5 computes the sum and calls `writeValue`).

Depends on: vtt-75c.16.

title: Formula: AST evaluation, scope, references, dispatch
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (literals), §2.1 (`and`, `or`, `not` short-circuit), §2.2 (roll result fields), §2.3 (`iserror`, origin, arity, unknown names), §3 (bare names, `this`, `it`, dot-access, references), §5 (`if`), as written by vtt-o9i.12.

`evaluate(ast, scope, env): Result` over vtt-o9i.3's `EvalEnv`, using vtt-o9i.6's value semantics, plus the function-call machinery vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8 plug into. Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/eval/scope.ts, evaluate.ts; src/functions/registry.ts, core.ts, library.ts and queries.ts (created as empty registrations, owned afterwards by vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8), src/index.ts (add this bead's export lines and preserve the lines already added by the parser, dice, host-interface and value-semantics beads; never reorder or remove them). This bead also edits test/support/fake-env.ts once: `FakeEnv.read` passes each value through vtt-o9i.6's `validateRefs` with its own `exists`. Tests: test/eval-*.test.ts with `FakeEnv`.

- Literals. `Dice {raw}` → `parseDice`; error → #TYPE, else a dice value with normalized `expr`. `Viewer` → viewers `["all"]` / `["gm"]`. `Record` → #TYPE in a formula (records exist only as `spawn` arguments; M5 reads their fields from the AST). Lists evaluate items left to right and go through `collectList`.
- Operators dispatch to vtt-o9i.6's `binary`/`unary` (passing `chained`). A new error gets `origin = scope.cell` when the scope names a cell.
- `a and b`: evaluate `a`; error → it; falsy → `a`; else evaluate and return `b` unchanged. `a or b`: error → it; truthy → `a`; else `b`. `not x`: error → it; else boolean. `if(c, x, y)`: exactly 3 args; `c` error → it; evaluate only the chosen branch and return it unchanged (a roll stays a roll). None of these broadcast.
- `iserror(x)` (core.ts, flagged `acceptsErrors`): true iff `x` is an error.
- Names and scope. `scope = {thisId, it?, itBindsNames?, cell?}`. `this` → `ref(thisId)`. `it` outside where/sort/objects → #NAME. A bare name reads `env.read(thisId, name)`; inside a predicate (`itBindsNames`) bare names resolve only against the item's cells, and an item that is not a ref makes a bare name #TYPE; `it` works for any item. `read` returning `undefined` → #NAME.
- Dot-access. On a ref: deleted (`!env.exists`) → #REF; else the named cell, absent → #NAME. On `empty` → `empty`. On a roll result: `total`, `dice`, `dropped` (lists of numbers), `expr` (a dice value); any other name → #NAME. On a list: apply to each item and flatten one level. Anything else → #TYPE.
- Function calls. The registry is injectable: `createRegistry(defs)`; `coreRegistry()` holds only core.ts entries (`if`, `iserror`); the default registry used by the package is core plus whatever library.ts and queries.ts register; `evaluate(ast, scope, env, registry = defaultRegistry)`. `FunctionDef {name, minArgs, maxArgs, kind: "eager" | "lazy", broadcast: "none" | "scalar", acceptsErrors?, impl}`. Eager args are evaluated left to right, then error-checked, then `impl` runs; `broadcast: "scalar"` maps over list arguments (several must have equal length, else #TYPE). Lazy functions receive ASTs plus an evaluation callback (used by `if`, and by `where`/`sort`/`objects`). Arity mismatch → #TYPE; unknown function → #NAME. `Method` nodes dispatch to registry entries `where`/`sort`; an absent entry → #NAME.
- Recursion is over the AST only and is bounded by the parser's depth limit (256) from vtt-o9i.4; `evaluate` must not overflow the JS stack on any AST the parser accepts.

Done when: tests cover every bullet (and must remain valid after vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8 register their functions), at least: `nickname or name` default; `if(bonus = empty, 0, bonus)`; `value + modifier` with both empty = 0; `if(true, r, 0)` deep-equals `r`; `and`/`or` with an error on either side; `if(iserror(x), 0, x)`; dot-access through a ref, on a list of refs (flattening a cell holding a list), on empty, on a deleted ref (#REF), on a roll result (`.total`, `.dice`, `.expr`, `.foo` #NAME); a dangling ref read from a cell inside a list is #REF through `FakeEnv`; bare name missing #NAME; `it` outside a predicate #NAME; arity mismatch #TYPE; unknown function #NAME; `x.where(...)` is #NAME when evaluated with `coreRegistry()` (an explicitly core-only registry, so the test stays valid after the library registers `where`); a call to a permanently unknown name (`no_such_function_zz(1)`) is #NAME with the default registry; error `origin` set from scope; parsing and evaluating a `1+1+…` chain and an `a.b.c…` chain at the parser's maximum depth gives a value (or a language error), never a stack exception; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); value semantics (vtt-o9i.6); the function library (vtt-o9i.7); queries (vtt-o9i.8); memoization, dependency recording, cycles (vtt-o9i.9), budgets (vtt-o9i.16).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.6, vtt-o9i.3, vtt-o9i.4, vtt-o9i.12.

Judgment calls accepted: LazyContext carries target and desc for methods (recorded in vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8 bead texts); where/sort as plain calls are #NAME; #NAME and arity checks precede argument evaluation; scalar broadcast recurses into nested lists; dot-access on lists flattens one level; errors read from other cells take this cell's origin only when they have none.

title: Formula: rolling and roll validation
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2.2 (rolling, roll results, keep/drop ranking, explosion and reroll rules as written by vtt-o9i.12); docs/FIXTURES.md §2 (roll result encoding), §5 (script entries are roll results to validate).

The random half of dice, on top of vtt-o9i.5's notation. Files: packages/formula/src/dice/roll.ts (and one added export line in src/dice/index.ts, which the package index already re-exports). Tests: test/dice-roll.test.ts.

- `RandomSource {int(min, max): number}` (inclusive, integers).
- `rollDice(dice, rng): RollValue`. Per term in order: roll `count` dice (1..S, or −1..1 for F). For each die in order: if a reroll condition holds, roll it once more; the new result replaces it and the original goes to `dropped` (no second reroll). Then if explode is on and the die shows S, roll an extra die, appended immediately after it; repeat while the extra shows S, at most 100 extras per original die; extras are separate dice and are not rerolled. Keep/drop then ranks all of the term's dice (including extras), ties broken by roll index ascending: `kh` and `dh` rank by value descending, `kl` and `dl` by value ascending; `kh`/`kl` keep the first N of the ranking, `dh`/`dl` drop the first N (so `dl1` drops the lowest die and `dh1` the highest). `dice` = kept dice of all terms in roll order; `dropped` = rerolled originals and keep/drop-dropped dice, in roll order; `total` = Σ sign × kept + constant; `expr` = normalized.
- `validateRoll(roll): string[]` checks a given roll result (from a fixture script or a replayed effect), per term. `expr` must parse. Terms are reconstructed in order from the flat `dice` and `dropped` lists: a term without explode or reroll contributes exactly its kept count (count, N for kh/kl, count − N for dh/dl) to `dice` and the rest of its count to `dropped`, so its boundaries are known. For every term whose boundaries are known: each kept and dropped die lies in that term's range (1..S, or −1..1 for F); counts match; keep/drop is consistent (kh: every kept ≥ every dropped of the term; kl: every kept ≤ every dropped; dh: every dropped ≥ every kept; dl: every dropped ≤ every kept). Validation proceeds term by term until the first term that explodes or rerolls; from there, boundaries are unknown, so each remaining die must lie in the union of the remaining terms' ranges, and the dropped count must be at least the remaining terms' keep/drop minimum. `total` is checked exactly whenever it is determined: always when every term has known boundaries, and also when every remaining term shares one sign (their kept dice sum with that sign). What cannot be verified, documented in the function's doc comment: which die belongs to which term, and the exact total, once exploding or rerolling pools of both signs appear together; whether an explosion or reroll actually happened.

Done when: with a scripted `RandomSource`: `4d6dl1` rolling 6,4,3,1 → `{dice:[6,4,3], dropped:[1], total:13}` (the FIXTURES §2 example); `4d6dh1` rolling 6,4,3,1 → dice [4,3,1], dropped [6]; `4d6kh3` rolling 6,4,3,1 → dice [6,4,3]; `4d6kl1` rolling 6,4,3,1 → dice [1]; ties for each of the four: `2d20kh1` rolling 7,7 keeps the first 7, `2d20kl1` rolling 7,7 keeps the first 7, `3d6dh1` rolling 5,5,2 drops the first 5, `3d6dl1` rolling 2,5,2 drops the first 2; explosion extras ranked with keep/drop for each mode (e.g. `2d6!kh1` rolling 6,3,2 ranks [6,3,2] and keeps 6; `2d6!dl1` rolling 6,1,4 drops 1); `1d6!` rolling 6,6,2 → dice [6,6,2], total 14; `1d6!` with a source that always returns 6 stops after 100 extras (101 dice); `1d20r<2` rolling 1 then 1 → dice [1], dropped [1]; `1d20-1d4` rolling 15,3 → total 12; `validateRoll` accepts every roll result in every fixture scenario's dice script and the `RollValue`s in its expectations (read with `node:fs` from packages/fixtures/scenarios/, no @vtt/fixtures import), and rejects: `{expr:"1d20", dice:[21]}`; a wrong total for `2d6+3`; `1d6+1d20` with kept `[20,1]` (per-term range); `2d6kh1` with kept `[1]`, dropped `[6]`, total 1 (keep consistency); `4d6dl1` with kept `[4,3,1]`, dropped `[6]`; a wrong kept count for `4d6dl1`; a die outside every remaining range after an exploding term; a wrong total for `1d20+1d6!` (same-sign remaining terms); and accepts an unverifiable-total case `1d6!-1d6!` while still checking ranges; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); notation, normalization, arithmetic, stats (vtt-o9i.5); the `roll` action step, dice sources and the dice script runner (vtt-75c.15, M5); cryptographic randomness.

Depends on: vtt-o9i.5.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Codex review: no in-scope findings. Decisions: reroll conditions compare strictly (recorded in FORMULAS §2.2 on the branch); the bead's total-check rule was corrected to 'every remaining term shares one sign'. Random draws settle each die (die, reroll, extras) before the next.

title: Docs: M1 language decisions
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2–§7 and DESIGN.md §10 (decision log) for every decision of the M1 plan, including the complete syntax contract; FIXTURES.md §4, §7, §11 and the fixtures `ErrorCodeSchema` for `#SYNTAX`.

Write every settled M1 language decision into the docs before any M1 implementation bead starts, so each implementation bead cites a doc section and none of them edits docs. This bead is the only M1 bead that touches FORMULAS.md, DESIGN.md, FIXTURES.md, or the fixture format. The parser bead (vtt-o9i.4) is explicitly authorized to run concurrently against the frozen syntax contract stated in its own text; this bead documents that same contract, and both must agree before milestone acceptance. The M2 docs bead (vtt-75c.2) runs after this one and must not rewrite these rows; decisions M2 owns (geometry module location and the geometry function contract, structural defaults, landing rules, undo, visibility, persistence, identity) are written by vtt-75c.2, not here.

Each item is an edit to the named section plus one decision-log row in DESIGN.md §10, dated 2026-11-05.

FORMULAS.md §2 (values):
1. `shape` is a value type: the value the structural `shape` cell reads as, `{type:"shape", shape}`; opaque to formulas (equality only, every other operation #TYPE; truthy); no literal syntax.
2. Value encoding: the language's values are the FIXTURES §2 tagged encoding plus the shape value and the error value `{type:"error", code, message?, origin?: {object, cell}}`; errors are never storable. Op records and the file reuse these types unchanged.
3. A ref to a deleted object read from a cell, directly or inside a list or a viewers value, makes the whole read #REF (visibility then fails closed).

FORMULAS.md §2.2 (dice and roll results):
4. Roll results outside arithmetic: they act as their total in arithmetic, comparison, numeric functions and `sum`/`avg`; render as their total in `&` and `text()`; are always truthy (a roll of total 0 is still rolled); `min`/`max`/`if`/`first`/`last` return the roll unchanged.
5. Dice dialect: lowercase `d`, uppercase `F`; each modifier kind at most once per pool, any input order; `khN`/`klN` need 1 ≤ N ≤ count, `dhN`/`dlN` need 1 ≤ N < count; count ≤ 1000, sides 2–1,000,000; no explode or reroll on `dF`; explosion extras are separate dice (not compounded), at most 100 per original die, not rerolled; reroll once, the original goes to `dropped`; keep/drop ranks all of a term's dice including extras: descending for `kh` and `dh`, ascending for `kl` and `dl`, ties by roll order; `kh`/`kl` keep the first N of that ranking and `dh`/`dl` drop the first N; `max_roll`/`min_roll` ignore explosion and rerolls; `sides` of `dF` is 3.
6. Normalized dice expression: explicit counts, modifiers in the order reroll, explode, keep/drop, integer constants folded into one trailing term, term order preserved (`1d6+1d20` ≠ `1d20+1d6`), no semantic simplification (`1d20kh1` ≠ `1d20`). Dice equality and fixture script matching use it.

FORMULAS.md §2.3 (errors):
7. `#SYNTAX`: the formula source does not parse, including exceeding the parser's limits (AST depth 256, counting every nesting including binary-operator and dot chains; 10,000 AST nodes) and a numeric literal that converts to a non-finite number.
8. Errors in lists: lists never contain errors; building a list from an error item yields that error; with several errors the first in evaluation order (left to right, list order) wins; origin is preserved through propagation.

FORMULAS.md §2 and §3 (syntax contract, complete, matching vtt-o9i.4):
9a. Whitespace (space, tab, newline) separates tokens; there are no comments. Numbers are `digits` or `digits.digits` (no exponent, no leading or trailing `.`); a number immediately followed by an identifier character is a syntax error; a numeric literal that converts to a non-finite number is a syntax error. Text is double-quoted with escapes `\"` and `\\` only; literal newlines allowed. Identifiers are `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, case-sensitive; backtick names are any non-empty text without a backtick and are always names (never keywords or dice). Dice literals follow the dialect of item 5 and win over identifiers when the following character is not an identifier character. Precedence, loosest to tightest: `or`; `and`; comparisons; `has`; `&`; `+ -`; `* / %`; prefix `-` and `not`; postfix call, dot, method; all left-associative; an unparenthesized comparison operand of a comparison is chained and evaluates to #TYPE. Records `{name: expr, …}` reject duplicate field names. A call is an identifier followed by `(`; the only methods are `.where(expr)` (exactly one argument) and `.sort(expr)` / `.sort(expr, desc)`; any other `.name(` is a syntax error. Limits as item 7.
9. Lexing and reserved words: `all` and `gm` are reserved viewer literals (`all(...)` is the aggregate call); `desc` is contextual, recognised only as `.sort(e, desc)`; `owner` in a formula is always the cell, never the symbolic `"owner"` viewer entry; `dS` is always a dice literal, so a cell named like dice needs backticks; `1d6!=3` is `1d6 != 3`.
10. Dot-access on `empty` is `empty` (a blank, not a typo).
11. Bare names inside `where`/`sort`/`objects` predicates resolve only against the item's cells (no fallback to `this`); a bare name when the item is not a ref is #TYPE; `it` works for any item.
12. `name` is literal-only in v1 (like `tag`): a formula on `name` or `tag` is refused by the store. `obj(x)`: an exact id wins; otherwise exact match over literal `name`s, which must match exactly one object (else #REF); the evaluating cell depends on the `name` cell of the object found and on the index.
13. `objects()` domain: every object in the document, including contained objects and templates.

FORMULAS.md §4 (operators):
14. `empty` in `< <= > >=` acts as 0 against numbers and roll results and as `""` against text; `empty` vs `empty` compares equal; `empty = 0` stays false.
15. Cross-kind equality: `=` never errors except on ink; different kinds are unequal (number vs roll compares the total); viewers compare as sets; `ink = x` is #TYPE unless `x` is `empty`; shapes compare structurally.
16. Numeric edge cases: IEEE doubles; `/0` and `%0` are #DIV0; any other non-finite result is #TYPE; `%` takes the sign of the dividend; `round` is half away from zero; `number()` accepts `-?digits(.digits)?` after trimming.
17. Text ordering is by Unicode code point, not UTF-16 unit.

FORMULAS.md §5 (conditionals, filtering, ordering):
18. `if` returns the chosen branch's value unchanged (a roll stays a roll).
19. Query order: results of `contents(zone)`, `zones_containing`, `on`, `objects` are ordered by ascending `z` (empty = 0), then id by code point; the evaluator sorts; "`contents`" in §5 means the function `contents(zone)`, while the `contents` cell keeps stored order. Candidates are evaluated in id code-point order before any geometry read or predicate, so which error a query returns does not depend on the host.
20. Errors in `where`/`sort`/`objects` predicates are strict: one item's error makes the whole result that error.

FORMULAS.md §6 (functions):
21. Aggregate call shape: exactly one argument; a scalar is a one-item list and `empty` is `[]` (`max(a, b)` is #TYPE: write `max([a, b])`); empty items are skipped by all aggregates except `len`; `min`/`max` return the item; `sum` of dice is #TYPE; `has` with an `empty` left side is false.
22. Spatial queries: the host supplies candidates and the evaluator computes membership, overlap and distance with the schema geometry. The candidate set is defined over literal geometry and is host-independent: every object placed directly on the board whose literal index bounds (the union of its footprint bounds and its anchor, expanded by the geometry epsilon) intersect the query bounds, plus every object on the board with any formula-valued geometry cell (`position`, `rotation`, `z`, `shape`; a cell with an override counts as literal) regardless of bounds. The host never evaluates formulas. The evaluator reads each candidate's geometry in id code-point order through ordinary (recorded) reads; an error from a geometry read, including #CYCLE, becomes the query's result; a successfully evaluated value that is not a valid position excludes the object. A spatial index is only a way of computing that set.
23. Exclusions: an object whose `position` is not two finite numbers is excluded from `contents`, `zones_containing` and `on` (not from `objects()`); a shapeless object has a point footprint, and `on()` counts a point footprint inside the other object's footprint as overlapping (the explicit exception to positive-area overlap).
24. `distance(a, b)` is Euclidean between anchors in raw board units; it is `empty` if either object is not on a board or has an invalid position, and #TYPE if they are on different boards; grid metrics and `unit` stay in §11.

FORMULAS.md §7 (evaluation model):
24a. `visible_to` is consumed through `toViewers`: the visibility code converts the evaluated `visible_to` value with `toViewers` (a viewers value as is; a ref to a character as a one-entry set; a list of refs and viewer sets as their union); anything that fails conversion (`empty`, an empty list, an error, another kind) admits nobody. So `visible_to = owner` and a list of character refs work as documented in §2.
25. Query dependencies are invalidated by changes to `position`, `rotation`, `shape`, `z`, `board`, `tag`, `container`, `is_zone`, `name`, creation, deletion (adds `name` and `is_zone`).
26. Budget (replaces any depth limit): each formula evaluation may spend 20,000 units; each cell read, each existence check, each candidate tested by a spatial query, and each id returned by `objects()`/`obj()` enumeration costs 1; reading an already computed dependency costs 1 regardless of its own cost. Because the candidate set is defined over literal geometry, the charge is the same on every host. Exceeding the budget is #LIMIT. There is no dependency-depth limit: the engine resolves dependencies iteratively, evaluates each dependency formula at most once per revision, and gives identical results across cold and warm caches and read orders.
27. Propagation is lazy pull with dirty marking: a commit marks dependents dirty once; the authority decides which cells to recompute and send.
28. The M1 fixture runner applies `set`, `override`, `clear_override`, `move`, checks `cell` and `cell_error`, and skips and reports everything else (DESIGN §10 row only).

FIXTURES.md and the fixture format: §4 replaces "once the language defines a parse-error code" with `#SYNTAX`; §7 lists `#SYNTAX` among `cell_error` codes; §11 records the additive `#SYNTAX` error code. This bead also makes the code change: add `#SYNTAX` to `ErrorCodeSchema` in packages/fixtures/src/schema.ts (the inferred type follows) and a case in packages/fixtures/test/format.test.ts accepting a `cell_error` with `#SYNTAX`. No scenario is edited. vtt-75c.2's fixture edits come after this bead.

Done when: each numbered item is present in the named section with its decision-log row dated 2026-11-05; the FIXTURES.md edits are present; `ErrorCodeSchema` accepts `#SYNTAX` and the format test covers it; no other test is required; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: any code other than the fixtures `ErrorCodeSchema` and its format test; M2's decisions (vtt-75c.2).

Depends on: none.

title: Authority: engine host adapter, recompute, visibility integration
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3 (names, `obj()` over literal names), §3.1 (structural cells readable, defaults), §6 (the literal-geometry candidate set), §7 (revision-consistent, dynamic and query dependencies, whole-document, cycles through geometry), as written by vtt-o9i.12 and vtt-75c.2; DESIGN.md §4.2, §4.4 (cover, fail closed), §7 (formulas evaluate only in the authority; internal synchronization before notifications).

Wire the M1 engine to the document. Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/engine/host.ts, table.ts, cover.ts, index.ts (one added export line in packages/authority/src/index.ts, never reordering others). Also switches the M1 test host to the canonical structural table (below).

- host.ts, `DocumentHost`: implements vtt-o9i.3's `EvalHost` over `DocumentStore` (vtt-75c.16) and `SpatialIndex` (vtt-75c.9); it never evaluates formulas: `exists` (boards exist; a missing id is how #REF arises); `cell` (stored content with an override returned as its literal; structural cells per `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` (vtt-75c.3): `id` text, `name` literal text, `tag` list of text, `contents` list of refs, derived `container` ref or empty, `board` ref or empty, `position` list of two numbers or formula or empty, `is_zone` boolean, `shape` a `ShapeValue` or empty); `objectsNamed` (exact match over literal `name`s); `allObjects`; `objectsOnBoard(board, near)` = `index.candidates(board, near)`, exactly the literal-geometry candidate set. Exact geometry is the evaluator's (vtt-o9i.8).
- cover.ts: `opaqueZonesCovering(obj)` returns `{covering, undetermined}` as vtt-75c.10 defines: for the object's (or outermost container's) board, consider every `is_zone` candidate of `index.candidates(board, anchorBox)` and every zone on the board with formula-valued geometry, `opaque` or `is_zone`; read `is_zone`, `opaque`, `position`, `rotation`, `shape` through `engine.value`; a zone whose reads are all valid, with `opaque` true and the anchor in its region (schema `pointInRegion`, vtt-75c.7), is `covering`; a zone with any read that is an error or of the wrong type is `undetermined` (fail closed).
- table.ts, `Table`: owns a store, an index, an engine (`createEngine(host)`, vtt-o9i.9, vtt-o9i.16), and a `Visibility` (vtt-75c.10) wired with `reader.value = engine.value` and the cover query. It registers one internal commit hook (`store.onCommitInternal`, vtt-75c.16), which runs before every public `onCommit` listener, including listeners registered before the table was constructed. From the commit payload `{group, summary}` the hook applies the commit to the index and builds the M1 `Change[]` from `summary.changedCells`, `summary.created` and `summary.removed` (all derived changes included: for a move, the object's `board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container` and both containers' `contents`; for create/remove, `object_created`/`object_deleted` for every object in the subtree plus the parent's `contents`; tag and shape field changes as `cell` changes; per-cell visibility changes produce none), then calls `engine.invalidate` once. `table.value(obj, cell)` = `engine.value`. `table.isOverridden(obj, cell)`. `Table.fromSnapshot`, `Table.fromStore`.

M1 test-host switch: packages/formula/test/support/memory-host.ts (vtt-o9i.15) imports `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` / `structuralDefault` from @vtt/schema instead of its own defaults, and the @vtt/formula tests stay green unchanged.

Done when: tests show: `hp = max_hp - damage_taken` recomputes after a `writeValue` commit and not before; an override shows instead of the formula result and clearing it resumes; a dice-tray zone sum (`sum(contents(this).where(tag has "die").value)`) follows a die moved in by `move`; `speed` follows a token moved into and out of a difficult zone; a parent formula over its `contents` (`len(contents)`) changes after a spawn into that container and after a remove from it; #REF after removing a referenced object and the value again after undo; a position formula following another object puts the follower in a zone's contents; two positions defined from each other give #CYCLE; `obj("Goblin")` resolves by name and changes after the goblin's `name` is rewritten; `shape` reads as a ShapeValue; a public `onCommit` observer registered on the store before `Table.fromStore` reads the new formula value (not a stale one) inside its callback; an object under a hidden opaque zone is not `canSeeObject` for a character through the real cover query, and a hidden zone whose `opaque` formula is an error also hides it; a `cell_visibility` change triggers no recomputation; `DocumentHost.objectsOnBoard` returns the same set as vtt-o9i.15's `literalCandidates` semantics for a random board including formula-positioned objects; the M1 test host imports the canonical table and no copy remains; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); action context and dice sources (vtt-75c.15); the action runner (M5); the WebSocket protocol and MCP server (M3); viewer filtering of query results (M3); finer index dependency keys (Polish).

Depends on: vtt-75c.9, vtt-75c.10, vtt-75c.8 (undo in tests); vtt-o9i.3, vtt-o9i.14, vtt-o9i.7, vtt-o9i.16.
