title: Formula: value semantics (coercion, operators, equality, broadcasting)
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (dangling refs), §2.1 (empty, truthiness, coercion), §2.2 (roll results in arithmetic and comparison; dice arithmetic; roll result fields), §2.3 (error propagation and first-error rule), §4 (all operators, equality, ordering, broadcasting), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.4 (viewer sets, `toViewers`).

The value semantics of the language, as pure functions over values: no AST, no environment, no scope. vtt-o9i.14 builds AST evaluation on top. Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/eval/values.ts, operators.ts, errors.ts, refs.ts. Tests: test/values-*.test.ts, all pure (no `FakeEnv`). Add this bead's `export * from` lines (values, operators, errors, refs, `toViewers`) to packages/formula/src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines.

- errors.ts: `firstError(...results)` (first error in argument order), `withOrigin(error, origin)` (sets origin only on a new error), the rule that any operator given an error operand returns that error unchanged (origin kept), and `collectList(items)`: a list built from items yields the first error in list order if any item is an error (lists never contain errors).
- values.ts: `truthy(v)` (`false`, `empty`, `0`, `""`, `[]` are false; everything else, including any ref, any roll result even of total 0, dice, viewers, ink, shape, is true); `toNumber` coercion for arithmetic (number; `empty` as 0; roll result as its total; anything else #TYPE); `toText(v)` (text as is, `empty` → `""`, number → JS `String(n)` with `-0` → `"0"`, boolean → `"true"`/`"false"`, dice → normalized notation, roll → its total as text; ref, viewers, ink, shape → #TYPE); `equals(a, b)`; `compare(a, b)` (code point order for text); `toViewers(v)`, the conversion the visibility code (vtt-75c.10) applies to every evaluated `visible_to` value (FORMULAS §2, decision written by vtt-o9i.12): a viewers value → itself; a ref → a one-entry set holding that ref (whether it names a character is the consumer's check); a list whose items are refs, viewers values, or nested such lists → the union of their entries, flattened, duplicates removed; `empty`, an empty list, an error, or any other kind → #TYPE (the consumer admits nobody). The evaluator never calls it.
- operators.ts: `binary(op, a, b)` and `unary(op, a)`, including broadcasting:
  - Arithmetic `+ - * / %`, unary `-`: operands through `toNumber`. Dice: `dice ± dice`, `dice ± number`, `number + dice`, `number - dice`, `-dice` give dice (vtt-o9i.5 `addDice`/`negateDice`; non-integer number → #TYPE); `empty` with dice acts as 0; a roll with dice acts as its total; `*`, `/`, `%` on dice → #TYPE. IEEE doubles; `/` and `%` by 0 → #DIV0; `%` takes the sign of the dividend; any other non-finite result → #TYPE. `"3" + 1` is #TYPE.
  - `&`: both operands through `toText`.
  - Equality `=`/`!=`: never #TYPE except ink: different kinds unequal, except number vs roll (total); numbers by value (`0 = -0`); text exact; booleans; `empty = empty` true, `empty = 0` and `empty = ""` false; refs by id; dice by normalized expr; roll vs roll by total; viewers as sets (order and duplicates ignored, refs by id); ink vs anything but `empty` → #TYPE; shapes structurally. Two lists → ordered recursive whole-list equality (a boolean). Exactly one list → broadcast.
  - Ordering `< <= > >=`: number/roll pairs (by total) and text pairs (code point order); `empty` acts as 0 against a number/roll and as `""` against text; `empty` vs `empty` equal; anything else (booleans, mixed number/text, refs, dice, shapes, …) → #TYPE; two lists → #TYPE; a node flagged `chained` → #TYPE (the AST bead passes the flag).
  - `has`: left a list → true iff some item `equals` the right (no broadcasting); left `empty` → false; any other left → #TYPE.
  - Broadcasting: for arithmetic, unary `-`, `&`, ordering, and equality with exactly one list: list ⊕ scalar and scalar ⊕ list elementwise; list ⊕ list of equal length elementwise for arithmetic and `&` (unequal → #TYPE); nested lists recursively; `[] ⊕ x` is `[]`. `has` and two-list `=`/`!=` never broadcast.
- refs.ts: `validateRefs(value, exists): Result`: if `value` is a ref, or contains a ref inside a list (at any depth) or a viewers value, whose object does not exist (`exists(id)` false), returns #REF; else the value unchanged. This is the single shared helper: vtt-o9i.14 wires it into `FakeEnv.read`, and the engine (vtt-o9i.9) calls it on every cell read, recording the existence checks as dependencies.

Done when: table-driven tests cover every bullet, at least: §2.1 examples (`"3" + 1` #TYPE, `empty = empty`, `empty = 0` false); empty + empty = 0, roll 14 + empty = 14, roll 11 + 5 = 16; `roll != empty` true; roll of total 28 `/ 2` = 14; `[roll15, num12] >= 13` = `[true, false]`; `[1,2] + [3,4]` = `[4,6]`, `[1,2] + [1]` #TYPE, `[1,2] = [1,2]` true, `[1,2] = 1` = `[true,false]`; `has` on a list of text; chained comparison #TYPE; error propagation through every operator, with two errors returning the first; `collectList` with an error item; `2d6 + 3` = dice `2d6+3`, `1d8 + 1d6 + 2`, `2 * 1d6` #TYPE, `1d6 + 0.5` #TYPE, `1d6 = d6` true; `1 / 0` #DIV0; `5 % -3` = 2; overflow to Infinity #TYPE; `toText` chain `"x" & 1 & true & empty & d6` = `"x1true1d6"`; text ordering by code point (`"Z" < "a"`, an astral character vs U+FFFF); two equal shapes equal, a shape `+ 1` #TYPE, a shape truthy, a roll of total 0 truthy; ink = ink #TYPE, ink = empty false; viewers set equality; `toViewers` cases: viewers as is, a single ref (the `visible_to = owner` shape), a list of two refs, a list mixing a ref and a viewers value, a nested list, duplicates removed, and #TYPE for `empty`, `[]`, a number, an error; `validateRefs` on a dangling ref, a dangling ref nested two lists deep, a dangling ref in a viewers value, and a live ref; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); AST evaluation, names, scope, dot-access, `if`/`and`/`or`/`not`, function dispatch (vtt-o9i.14); the function library (vtt-o9i.7); queries (vtt-o9i.8); the engine (vtt-o9i.9); effective visibility composition (vtt-75c.10).

title: Formula: dice notation, normalization, arithmetic, statistics
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2.2 (dice values, modifiers, arithmetic, dice functions; the dice dialect and normalization as written by vtt-o9i.12), §4 (dice equality by normalized expression); docs/FIXTURES.md §5 (script entries match by normalized expression).

The pure, non-random half of dice: grammar, canonical form, arithmetic, and static functions. The evaluator depends only on this half; rolling is vtt-o9i.13. Files: packages/formula/src/dice/notation.ts, arith.ts, stats.ts, index.ts (this bead's exports; vtt-o9i.13 adds its own export lines without reordering). Tests: test/dice-notation.test.ts, test/dice-arith.test.ts, test/dice-stats.test.ts. Add `export * from "./dice/index"` to packages/formula/src/index.ts (Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines; vtt-o9i.14 preserves them). Fixture access: the test that parses every dice-script `expr` reads packages/fixtures/scenarios/*.json directly with `node:fs` (path relative to the test file) and does not import @vtt/fixtures.

notation.ts: `parseDice(expr): DiceExpr | DiceError` over `DiceExpr = {terms: DiceTerm[], constant: number}`, `DiceTerm = {sign: 1|-1, count, faces: number | "F", reroll?: {op:"<"|">"|"=", n}, explode: boolean, keep?: {mode:"kh"|"kl"|"dh"|"dl", n}}`. Grammar:

```
expr     := ws? ["-"] item (ws? ("+"|"-") ws? item)* ws?
item     := pool | integer
pool     := [count] "d" (sides | "F") modifier*
modifier := ("kh"|"kl"|"dh"|"dl") integer | "!" | "r" ("<"|">"|"=") integer
```

Lowercase `d`, uppercase `F` only. Validation (each failure a `DiceError` with a message; the evaluator turns it into #TYPE): count 1–1000; sides 2–1,000,000; at least one pool; at most one modifier of each kind (keep/drop counts as one kind), any input order; `khN`/`klN` need 1 ≤ N ≤ count; `dhN`/`dlN` need 1 ≤ N < count; `!` and `r` not allowed on `dF`; reroll `n` within 1..sides. Integers are summed into `constant`.

`normalizeDice(expr): string`: terms in source order (never reordered); count always explicit (`d20` → `1d20`, `dF` → `1dF`); modifiers in the order reroll, explode, keep/drop (`1d6kh1!` → `1d6!kh1`); no semantic simplification (`1d20kh1` stays); constants folded into one trailing signed integer, omitted if 0 (`2+1d6+1` → `1d6+3`); no spaces; first term carries `-` only if negative. `diceEquals(a, b)` compares normalized strings. `renderDice(DiceExpr)` is the inverse of `parseDice` on canonical input.

arith.ts: `addDice(a, b)` where `b` is a `DiceExpr` (terms concatenated, constants summed) or an integer (non-integer → error); `negateDice(a)` (every term's sign and the constant flipped). `number + dice` equals `dice + number` after normalization.

stats.ts: `maxRoll`, `minRoll`, `faces`, `sides`. Max/min ignore explosion and rerolls and respect keep/drop: a positive pool contributes `kept × S` (max) / `kept × 1` (min) where `kept` = count, or N for kh/kl, or count − N for dh/dl; `dF` contributes `+kept` / `−kept`; a negative pool contributes the negated opposite bound; plus the constant (`maxRoll("4d6dl1") = 18`, `minRoll("1d20-1d4") = -3`). `faces` = sum of counts over all pools. `sides` = each pool's sides repeated `count` times, in term order; `dF` counts as 3.

Done when: each §2.2 example parses and normalizes (`2d6+3`, `1d20kh1`, `4d6dl1`, `1d6!`, `2d20kl1`, `dF`, `d20`, `1d20r<2`, `1d8+3`, `8d6`); the normalization cases above hold; `diceEquals("1d8+3", "1d8 + 3")` and `diceEquals("d20", "1d20")` true, `diceEquals("1d6+1d20", "1d20+1d6")` false; every validation failure above is rejected with a message; `addDice("1d8", "1d6")` + 2 → `1d8+1d6+2`; `negateDice("1d6+2")` → `-1d6-2`; the stats examples above; every `expr` in every fixture scenario's dice script parses; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); rolling and roll validation (vtt-o9i.13); the formula lexer (vtt-o9i.4); dice under formula operators (vtt-o9i.6); the dice script runner (vtt-75c.15, M5); compound explosions and success counting (FORMULAS §11).

title: Formula: lexer and Pratt parser
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (literal syntax, including record literals), §2.3 (#SYNTAX and the parser limits), §2.2 (dice literal syntax, as tokens), §3 (names, `this`, `it`, dot-access, backtick names), §4 (operators, precedence, non-chaining comparisons), §5 (`if`, `.where`, `.sort`, `desc`), §6 (call syntax).

Hand-written lexer and Pratt parser producing an AST. No evaluation, no schema dependency.

Files: packages/formula/src/syntax/tokens.ts, lexer.ts, ast.ts, parser.ts; tests test/lexer.test.ts, test/parser.test.ts.

Lexical rules (state them in lexer.ts comments):

- Whitespace (space, tab, newline) separates tokens and is otherwise ignored. No comments.
- Numbers: `digits` or `digits.digits`. No exponent, no leading `.`, no trailing `.`. A number immediately followed by an identifier character is a syntax error (`2x`). A numeric literal that converts to a non-finite number (e.g. a 400-digit literal) is a parse failure, which the engine reports as #SYNTAX.
- Text: double-quoted; escapes `\"` and `\\` only; any other backslash sequence is an error; literal newlines allowed; unterminated is an error.
- Identifiers: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, case-sensitive. Backtick names `` `...` `` (no backtick inside, non-empty) are always names, never keywords or dice.
- Keywords: `true false empty this it all gm and or not has`. `all` and `gm` are reserved: bare, they are viewer literals; `all(` is the aggregate call. `desc` is not a keyword (it is a likely cell name): it is recognised only as the bare second argument of `.sort`. `owner` is an ordinary name (the cell), never the symbolic `"owner"` viewer entry, which exists only in stored literals.
- Dice literals: at a digit or `d`, try `[0-9]*d([0-9]+|F)` followed by modifiers `(kh|kl|dh|dl)[0-9]+`, `!`, `r(<|>|=)[0-9]+`, in any order. It is a dice token only if the character after the match is not `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; otherwise fall back (`d6x` is an identifier, `2d6kh` is a syntax error). A `!` immediately followed by `=` is never consumed as explode (`1d6!=3` is `1d6 != 3`). The token carries the raw text; vtt-o9i.5 validates it. Consequently a cell named `d6` or `dF` must be backticked.
- Punctuation: `+ - * / % & = != < <= > >= ( ) [ ] { } , . :` and `->` (lexed for M5's step syntax; the expression parser rejects it).

Grammar and precedence, loosest to tightest: `or`; `and`; comparisons `= != < <= > >=`; `has`; `&`; `+ -`; `* / %`; prefix `-` and `not`; postfix (call `f(...)`, dot `.name`, method `.where(...)`/`.sort(...)`). All binary operators are left-associative. Comparisons are parsed left-associatively but a comparison node whose unparenthesized left or right operand is itself a comparison is flagged `chained: true`; the evaluator returns #TYPE for it (§4). `(a = b) = c` is not chained.

AST node kinds (ast.ts, each with `start`/`end` offsets): `Number`, `Text`, `Boolean`, `Empty`, `Dice {raw}`, `Viewer {which: "all"|"gm"}`, `This`, `It`, `Name {name}`, `List {items}`, `Record {fields: [name, expr][]}` (duplicate field names are a syntax error), `Unary {op}`, `Binary {op, chained?}`, `Dot {target, name}`, `Call {name, args}`, `Method {target, name: "where"|"sort", args, desc: boolean}`. A call is an identifier (not a backtick name) followed by `(`, whitespace allowed. `.name(` where `name` is not `where`/`sort` is a syntax error. `.sort(e, desc)` sets `desc: true`; any other second argument, or more than two arguments, is a syntax error. `.where` takes exactly one argument. Functions are not resolved here (unknown names are #NAME at evaluation, §2.3) and arity is not checked here.

Entry points: `parse(source): ParseResult` (whole input must be one expression; failure is `{ok:false, message, offset}` with no partial AST), and `parseExpressionPrefix(source, start): {ok, ast, end} | failure`, which stops at the first token that cannot continue the expression (for M5's step parser). A parse failure becomes the error value #SYNTAX in the engine (vtt-o9i.9); the parser itself only returns the failure.

Limits (FORMULAS §2.3 as written by vtt-o9i.12): the AST depth is at most 256, counting every nesting level, including each level of a left-associative binary chain (`1+1+…`), each postfix dot, call or method (`a.b.c…`), parentheses, lists, records, and unary chains; and the AST has at most 10,000 nodes. Exceeding either is a parse failure whose message names the limit. Both limits apply to `parseExpressionPrefix` too. The parser tracks depth while parsing, so it reports the failure without overflowing the JS stack. These limits are what bound the evaluator's recursion over the AST.

Done when: every formula source and every `when` source in every scenario under packages/fixtures/scenarios/ parses (the test discovers them); each §10 formula in FORMULAS.md parses to the expected tree (snapshot of a compact s-expression printer `printAst` written in this bead), including `any(on(this).where(tag has "d20").total >= ac)` (method on call, dot on method, `>=` loosest inside the call) and `roll != empty and total >= target.ac`; precedence cases: `not a = b` is `(= (not a) b)`, `-x.y` is `(neg (. x y))`, `a & b has c` is `(has (& a b) c)`, `1 + 2 * 3`, `a or b and c`; `a < b < c` parses with `chained: true`; dice tokens `2d6`, `d20`, `dF`, `1d20kh1`, `4d6dl1`, `1d6!`, `2d20kl1`, `1d20r<2`, `` `d6` `` (a name), `d6x` (a name), `1d6!=3` (dice, `!=`, number); `2d6+3` is `(+ (dice 2d6) 3)`; record `{target: it, owner: it.owner}`; `x.sort(y, desc)` sets desc and a cell named `desc` parses as a name elsewhere; syntax errors with offsets for `2x`, `"a\q"`, `"abc`, `(1`, `a.b(1)`, `[1,]`, `x.sort(y, up)`, `{a: 1, a: 2}`; limits: 256 nested parentheses parse and 257 fail; a `1+1+…` chain 256 levels deep parses and one 257 levels deep fails with the depth message; a 300-level `a.b.c…` chain fails; a flat list literal with more than 10,000 nodes fails with the node-count message; a 100,000-term `1+1+…` source returns a failure, never a stack exception. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (the lexical decisions and limits are written by vtt-o9i.12; this bead edits no docs); evaluation; dice semantics beyond tokenizing (vtt-o9i.5); action step syntax (`->`, step names, cell paths, destinations: M5); mapping parse failures to #SYNTAX (vtt-o9i.9).

Depends on: none. Every lexical rule and limit is stated above, so this bead does not wait for vtt-o9i.12.
notes: Codex review: no findings. AST notes for vtt-o9i.6/.14: no Paren node (offsets widened); chained:true only when set; -2 is Unary over Number; Method.args is exactly one expr with desc as a boolean; Call.name may be 'all'; if() arrives as a plain Call and must be special-cased; Record.fields ordered pairs; Dice.raw unvalidated; non-finite numeric literal is a lex failure. Depth: leaf 0, each nesting level +1, parentheses add a level.

title: Formula: evaluation host interface, FakeEnv, fixture conversion
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3 (literal-only `name`), §3.1 (structural cells and defaults), §6 (spatial candidate set), §7 (query dependencies, budget, viewer-independence), as written by vtt-o9i.12 and vtt-75c.2; DESIGN.md §4.3; docs/FIXTURES.md §2, §3.

The boundary between the pure language and the document, plus the stateless test doubles. The mutable test document is vtt-o9i.15. M2's engine adapter (vtt-75c.12) implements `EvalHost` over the document store.

packages/formula/src/host.ts (types plus doc comments that are the contract):

- `EvalHost`, a view of one revision of the raw document; it never evaluates formulas:
  - `exists(id): boolean`: object (or board) exists at this revision.
  - `cell(id, name): CellContent | undefined`: stored content; an override is returned as its literal; unstored structural cells read as their default (table below); `undefined` = no such cell.
  - `objectsNamed(name): ObjectId[]`: exact match over literal `name`s (`name` is literal-only).
  - `allObjects(): ObjectId[]`: every object in the document.
  - `objectsOnBoard(board, near: Bounds): ObjectId[]`: the candidate set, defined over literal geometry (FORMULAS §6): every object placed directly on `board` (never inside a container) whose literal `indexBounds` (vtt-75c.7: union of footprint bounds and anchor, expanded by epsilon) intersect `near` (inclusive), plus every object on `board` with any formula-valued geometry cell (`position`, `rotation`, `z`, `shape`; a cell with an override counts as literal) regardless of bounds. Each id once, any order. An object whose literal position is not two finite numbers is not a candidate by bounds (the evaluator would exclude it).
  Contract: the host never filters by visibility; result ordering and exact tests are the evaluator's (vtt-o9i.8).
- `EvalEnv`, what the evaluator sees (implemented by the engine, by M2's action context vtt-75c.15, by `FakeEnv`): `read(id, cell): Result | undefined`, `exists`, `objectsNamed`, `allObjects`, `objectsOnBoard(board, near)`.
- `Change = {type:"cell", object, cell} | {type:"object_created", object} | {type:"object_deleted", object}`; `CellKey` (object id + cell name with an unambiguous separator); `Dependency = {type:"cell", object, cell} | {type:"exists", object} | {type:"index"}`.

Structural cell value shapes and defaults (canonical: `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` in @vtt/schema, vtt-75c.3; stated here so M1 and M2 agree; FORMULAS §3.1 as written by vtt-75c.2):

| Cell | Reads as | Default when not stored |
|---|---|---|
| id | text | (always present) |
| name | text, literal only | empty |
| tag | list of text, literal only | [] |
| visible_to | viewers | viewers ["all"] |
| owner, template | ref or empty | empty |
| contents | list of refs, stored order | [] |
| container | ref or empty (derived) | empty |
| board | ref or empty | empty (in a container) |
| position | list of two numbers, or a formula | empty (in a container) |
| rotation | number (degrees clockwise about the anchor, y down) | empty (read as 0) |
| z | number | empty (read as 0) |
| face_up | boolean | true |
| opaque | boolean | false |
| is_zone | boolean | false |
| shape | ShapeValue | empty (no shape) |

`is_template` and `is_character` are object fields, not readable cells.

packages/formula/test/support/:

- fake-env.ts: `FakeEnv` implements `EvalEnv` from a plain map `{[id]: {[cell]: Result}}` plus optional stubbed answers for `objectsOnBoard` (map board → ids), `objectsNamed`, `allObjects`. No formulas. Its `read` returns map values as given; dangling-ref validation is added by vtt-o9i.14 through vtt-o9i.6's shared helper.
- fixture-values.ts: `fromFixtureValue(v): Value` and `fromFixtureContent(c): CellContent`: a checked cast through `isValue`.
- scenarios.ts: `loadScenarios()`: every scenario in packages/fixtures/scenarios/, discovered via `import.meta.resolve("@vtt/fixtures")` → `../scenarios`, parsed with the fixtures loader.

Package setup: add `"@vtt/fixtures": "workspace:*"` to @vtt/formula devDependencies and `"@vtt/schema": "workspace:*"` to its dependencies (lockfile rides along). Add this bead's `export * from` lines (host types) to packages/formula/src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines.

Done when: test/host-types.test.ts: type-level tests (`expectTypeOf`) for `EvalHost`, `EvalEnv`, `Change`, `Dependency`; `FakeEnv` returns mapped values, `undefined` for missing cells, and stubbed query answers; test/fixture-values.test.ts: every literal value anywhere in every scenario (setup cells, step values, expectation values, dice script entries) passes `isValue` through `fromFixtureValue`, and a deliberately malformed value throws; `loadScenarios()` returns all ten scenarios; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); the mutable test document (vtt-o9i.15); exact spatial tests (vtt-o9i.8) and geometry (vtt-75c.7); the engine (vtt-o9i.9); any evaluation; visibility.

Depends on: vtt-o9i.2, vtt-o9i.12, vtt-75c.2.

title: Schema: cell value types
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (value table, including the shape value), §2.2 (roll result parts), §2.3 (error codes, including #SYNTAX), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.4 (viewer sets); docs/FIXTURES.md §2 (encodings).

Create the value types every other package shares. Small and first: M2's schema bead (vtt-75c.3) and M1's host, dice, and value-semantics beads depend on it. The value types are the FIXTURES §2 tagged JSON encoding plus the shape value and the error value (FORMULAS §2, §2.3).

Files in packages/schema/src/:

- ids.ts: `ObjectId = string`; `ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/` (the fixtures `NameSchema` pattern); `isIdSyntax(s)`. vtt-75c.3 later adds reserved ids and board ids to this file and imports `ID_PATTERN` from here.
- values.ts: one exported type per kind, tagged on `type`, field names and JSON shapes identical to packages/fixtures/src/types.ts: `NumberValue {value}`, `TextValue {value}`, `BooleanValue {value}`, `EmptyValue`, `ListValue {items: Value[]}`, `RefValue {object: ObjectId}`, `DiceValue {expr}`, `RollValue {expr, dice: number[], dropped: number[], total}`, `ViewersValue {viewers: ViewerEntry[]}` with `ViewerEntry = "all" | "gm" | "owner" | RefValue`, `InkValue {strokes: Point[][]}`, `ShapeValue {type:"shape", shape: Shape}`. `Value` is their union. `ErrorCode` string union and `ERROR_CODES` array: `#CYCLE #NAME #TYPE #REF #DIV0 #LIMIT #SYNTAX`. `ErrorValue {type:"error", code, message?: string, origin?: {object, cell}}`. `Result = Value | ErrorValue`. Constructors `num`, `text`, `bool`, `EMPTY`, `list`, `ref`, `dice`, `shape`, `err(code, message?, origin?)`, and `isError(r)`.
- shape.ts: `Point = [number, number]`; `Shape = {type:"rect", width, height} | {type:"circle", radius} | {type:"polygon", points: Point[]}`; `Bounds = {minX, minY, maxX, maxY}` (axis-aligned box in board units; used by the host interface vtt-o9i.3 and returned by the schema geometry vtt-75c.7).
- cell.ts: `FormulaContent {type:"formula", source}`; `CellContent = Value | FormulaContent`.
- guard.ts: `isValue(x: unknown): x is Value` and `isCellContent`, hand-written, no dependencies. Contract, field by field (every object strict: an unknown key fails; `type` must be a known tag):
  - number: `value` a finite number (NaN and ±Infinity rejected).
  - text: `value` a string (may be empty).
  - boolean: `value` a boolean. empty: no other fields.
  - list: `items` an array of values (recursive; may be empty); an error item fails.
  - ref: `object` a string matching `ID_PATTERN`.
  - dice: `expr` a string that is not blank after trimming (its grammar is not checked here).
  - roll: `expr` non-blank; `dice` and `dropped` arrays of integers; `total` a finite number.
  - viewers: `viewers` a non-empty array of `"all"`, `"gm"`, `"owner"`, or ref values.
  - ink: `strokes` a non-empty array of non-empty arrays of points; a point is a two-element array of finite numbers.
  - shape: rect with finite `width`, `height`; circle with finite `radius`; polygon with an array of points (positivity and simplicity are document invariants checked by vtt-75c.3).
  - `type:"error"` is rejected (errors are not storable).
  - `isCellContent`: a value, or `{type:"formula", source}` with `source` non-blank after trimming.
- index.ts: one `export * from "./<module>.ts"` line per module. Rule for every bead that touches this package index: add only your own export lines, never reorder or edit others'.

The schema package must not import @vtt/fixtures (not even as a dev dependency). Conformance against real fixture values is tested in vtt-o9i.3. Zod schemas are not part of this bead; vtt-75c.3 adds zod wrappers that delegate to `isValue`.

Done when: test/values.test.ts round-trips one example of every kind (including shape) through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` and `isValue`; negative tests, one each: NaN and Infinity in a number, a roll total, a die result (and a non-integer die), an ink point, a shape dimension; a ref whose id breaks `ID_PATTERN` (`"1abc"`, `"a-b"`, `""`); blank dice `expr` and blank roll `expr`; a viewers value with no entries and with an unknown entry; ink with no strokes and with an empty stroke; a formula with blank source (via `isCellContent`); an error value; a list containing an error; an unknown `type`; an extra key; a type-level test (`expectTypeOf`) shows `Result` = `Value | ErrorValue`; `ERROR_CODES` has exactly the seven codes; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (written by vtt-o9i.12); document, object, operation and protocol types (vtt-75c.3, vtt-75c.4); zod (vtt-75c.3); geometry (vtt-75c.7); dice grammar (vtt-o9i.5); equality and coercion (vtt-o9i.6); the fixtures `ErrorCodeSchema` (vtt-o9i.10).

Depends on: vtt-o9i.12.

title: Fixture scenario format
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 (notation and intent), §2 (values), §3.1 (structural cells), §8 (actions, whole section), DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects, containment), §4.4 (visibility), §7 (operations, undo).

Design the machine-readable form of the §10 fixtures in packages/fixtures. Deliver TypeScript types, a zod validator, docs/FIXTURES.md, and tests. This bead owns the format; transcription beads may not change it. A scenario must be able to express everything below.

Table setup. Objects with unique id, tags, cells, and ordered `contents` (owning, acyclic). `container` is derived from contents, never written. An object is either in a container or placed on a board (board id, position, and shape for zones and tokens), never both. Non-owning references are a tagged value. Templates are objects marked as templates; instances are made from them by a spawn step. Per-cell visibility as in DESIGN §4.4.

Cell values. Every §2 storable value has an unambiguous tagged encoding: number, text, boolean, empty, reference, dice expression, roll result (with its parts), viewer set, ink. Formula source is a separate tagged form from literal text. Errors are expectations, never setup values.

Dice script. An ordered list of roll results consumed in order during execution. Exhaustion is a scenario error. The script is execution input only; it is not a replay mechanism (DESIGN §7 replays recorded effects). Shuffle takes an explicit permutation from the script.

Actions on an object: name, optional `when` source, ordered steps as source text. Steps performed by an actor (GM or a named viewer): set literal, override a formula cell, clear override, invoke action, move object to board position, move object into a container at an index, spawn template into a container or onto a board with initial cells and a symbolic binding for the new object (and for objects it owns), undo last action group.

Expectations after any step: cell value, cell error code, cell has override marker, action enabled or disabled, action invocation rejected with a reason and no state change, object exists or has been removed (recursively), object container and index, object board placement, ordered contents of an object, cell visible or hidden to a named viewer, object visible or hidden to a named viewer, number of log groups, and that the latest log group's resolved effects include a given cell write or roll.

A test/scenarios.test.ts that discovers every file under scenarios/ and validates it; it passes trivially now. docs/FIXTURES.md with the format walkthrough and one stub section per §10 fixture, each with a link slot the transcription beads fill in.

Done when: docs/FIXTURES.md walks through every §10 fixture and shows how the format expresses each behaviour the prose calls out, with no unexpressible construct remaining; validator and sample tests pass; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check pass.

Out of scope: transcribing the remaining fixtures; any evaluator, parser, or runner; replay expectations (M2 extends the format additively); face layout and show-when (M5 extends the format additively); depending on the schema package.

title: Workflow scripts: worktree, bead review, plan review
description:
Implements: CLAUDE.md Loop per implementation bead and Tracking: beads.

Add scripts/ (bash, no build step) that encode the loop:
- scripts/worktree.sh <bead-id> <slug>: creates branch <bead-id>/<slug> from main in ../vtt-worktrees/<bead-id>, runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile there, and verifies bd works from inside the worktree with bd show <bead-id> (bd 1.3.4 already finds the main repo's .beads from a worktree; the script only needs to check, and fail loudly if it does not).
- scripts/review-bead.sh <bead-id> [base=main]: builds a review prompt from bd show <bead-id> plus a reminder that findings are advisory and must each be tagged IN-SCOPE or OUT-OF-SCOPE and that the review must state whether every Done-when condition is met, appends git diff <base>...HEAD excluding pnpm-lock.yaml in a fenced block, and runs `codex exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check -o <outfile> -` with that prompt on stdin from the current worktree. Do NOT use `codex review`: it rejects a custom prompt together with --base. Prints the review to stdout and saves it under .reviews/<bead-id>-<timestamp>.md (already gitignored).
- scripts/review-plan.sh <epic-id>: dumps the epic and each child via bd show, with a prompt asking for missing dependencies, overlapping scope, oversized beads, gaps against named doc sections, and bad decisions, each finding with bead id, severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), problem, and proposed change, ending with an overall verdict. Each script has a usage line, uses set -euo pipefail, and fails loudly on missing tools (bd, codex, pnpm, git). Scripts touch only scripts/ and a Workflow section appended to README.md.

Done when: each script runs end to end against a throwaway bead (create one with bd create, delete it with bd delete afterwards) in a throwaway worktree that is removed afterwards; pnpm lint and format:check pass; the README documents the three commands.

Out of scope: CI, automated merging, bead closing, anything that edits beads other than the throwaway.

description:

Markdown formatting off (the design docs are not reformatted); tool-managed folders (.beads, .agents, .claude, .codex, .cursor) excluded; ignoreUnknown on.
- .nvmrc / .node-version at the installed major (Node 26). .editorconfig. README.md with two lines pointing at docs/ and CLAUDE.md. Extend .gitignore with .reviews/.
- Add a Conventions subsection to CLAUDE.md: run pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test before asking for review; libraries are source-consumed; one vitest.config.ts per package.

Done when: fresh clone, pnpm install, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test all exit 0 with zero packages present; introducing an unused variable in a scratch .ts file makes pnpm lint fail.

title: Epic acceptance: §8.4 step 5 headless
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §8.4 step 5 ("Through the MCP server, ask the agent: 'Make room 4 difficult terrain and hatch it, and make a Fireball card for Aldric with DC 14 and 8d6.' Check its work in the inspector. Correct the DC by typing over it."), §5.2, §4.4; FORMULAS.md §10 (Difficult terrain, Fireball); docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (stale writes, undo targets), §8, §11; the epic vtt-5su Done-when.

The epic acceptance test, black box: the authority and the MCP server run as the real binaries (`vtt-serve` from vtt-5su.14, `vtt-mcp` from vtt-5su.17). Exclusive files: `packages/authority/test/acceptance/step5.test.ts`, `prep.ts`, `agent-script.ts`. The agent is a deterministic script (no model) doing what an agent would.

1. Start `vtt-serve <tmp>/crypt.table.json --port 0 --print-session` as a subprocess (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in a temp directory); read `{url, token}`.
2. `prep.ts`, as the GM through a `ProtocolClient` (`kind: "ui"`): board `crypt` "Crypt"; character `aldric` (`is_character`) on `gm_board` with `aldric_binder` (owner `aldric`, `visible_to` owner) on `gm_board`; six zones `room1`…`room6` on `crypt` (`is_zone`, rect shapes, `opaque: true`, `visible_to` gm, names "Room 1"…"Room 6"); a token `pc1` (tag `creature`, `base_speed: 30`, the `speed` formula of FORMULAS §10 Difficult terrain) inside room 4; a goblin `goblin1` (tag `creature`) in room 3.
3. Start `vtt-mcp --url … --token … --name step5-agent` through the MCP SDK's stdio client transport. `agent-script.ts`: `table_info`; `zones {board:"crypt"}` → the zone named "Room 4"; `transact` (label "Room 4: difficult terrain, hatched"): `set_tag room4 ["difficult"]`, `set_value room4.pattern "hatch"` (the hatch is an ordinary cell; M4 decides appearance cells); `get_objects ["pc1"]` → `speed` 15; `transact` (label "Fireball card for Aldric"), one group: `create_object fireball_aldric` into `aldric_binder` with cells `name "Fireball"`, `owner` and `caster` ref `aldric`, `zone` ref `fireball_aldric_zone`, `dc 14`, `damage_dice 8d6`, `damage` empty, `locked false`, `applied false`, `save_row` ref `fireball_save_row`, formulas `targets = contents(zone).where(tag has "creature")` and `rows = contents.where(tag has "save_row")`, and the four actions of FORMULAS §10 Fireball with Roll damage as `roll(damage_dice) -> damage`; `create_object fireball_aldric_zone` into `fireball_aldric` (`is_zone`, a circle shape); `create_object fireball_save_row` into `aldric_binder` (`is_template`, tag `save_row`; cells `target` empty and `save_roll` empty; formulas `card = container`, `save_bonus = target.dex_save`, `passed = save_roll + save_bonus >= card.dc`, `damage_dealt = if(passed, floor(card.damage / 2), card.damage)`; action `Roll save` with `when: save_roll = empty` and steps `["roll(1d20) -> save_roll"]`, all per FORMULAS §10 Fireball); `explain_action` for each of the card's four actions and for the row template's `Roll save` (no `when_error` with `#SYNTAX`); `explain_cell fireball_aldric.targets` while the zone is still inside the card: value `[]`, and the recorded dependencies are cell dependencies only, with no `index` node (`contents(zone)` of a contained zone asks for no board candidates; dependencies are recorded dynamically, FORMULAS §7); then `transact` `move fireball_aldric_zone` onto `crypt` at a point outside every room, `explain_cell fireball_aldric.targets` now lists an `index` dependency, and `undo {type:"mine"}` puts the zone back inside the card (asserted with `get_objects`).
4. Check its work, as the GM: `get_objects` shows the zone, card, row template and every cell as written; the card group is one group whose actor is `{type:"agent", name:"step5-agent"}`; a subscription with scope `all` and viewer Aldric contains the card and its zone, no room zone, six covers on `crypt`, and no `pc1` (covered); the GM `spawn`s `fireball_save_row` into `fireball_aldric` (as `$row`), `get_objects` on the copy shows the `Roll save` action with its `when` and steps and every row cell, the card's `rows` lists the copy, and the GM then undoes that spawn (`undo {type:"mine"}`) so the remaining steps start from the agent's card (invoking `Roll save` stays M5).
5. Correct the DC by typing over it: the agent subscribes to `{type:"objects", ids:["fireball_aldric"]}` beforehand; the GM `transact`s `set_value fireball_aldric.dc 15`; the agent's `poll_changes` returns that cell change with actor `gm`; the agent's `transact` with its old `base_revision` writing `dc` is rejected `stale_write` naming the GM's group; the agent's `undo {type:"group", index: <card group index>}` is refused `undo_conflict` (the GM's later `dc` write touches the card); then the agent's `transact` writing `damage_dice 10d6` with the same old base commits; finally the agent's `undo {type:"mine", expect_index: <card group index>}` is refused `undo_target_changed` with `actual` = the `damage_dice` group's index (its newest group).
6. `save`; SIGTERM the server; restart it on the same file with `--port <same port> --token <same token>`; the MCP process reconnects; the agent's `poll_changes` on its subscription handle returns a `resync` record with `session_changed: true`; the agent's next `get_objects ["fireball_aldric"]` shows `dc 15`, `damage_dice 10d6`, and the four actions; `log` lists the agent's groups with their actor.

Done when: `step5.test.ts` passes within 60 s and leaves no subprocess or lock file behind (asserted in `afterAll`); its header comment quotes §8.4 step 5 and maps each sentence to the numbered blocks above; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: a model in the loop; the inspector UI (M4); invoking the card's actions (M5); hatch rendering (M4).

title: Authority: fixture scenarios over the protocol
description:
Implements: FIXTURES.md §1–§8, §11 (as amended by vtt-75c.2); DESIGN.md §5.2 (the agent and the UI go "through the same invariants"); the M2 runner contract (vtt-75c.13, including its `onStep` observation hook); docs/PROTOCOL.md §4–§8 as written by vtt-5su.2; FORMULAS.md §7 (the maintained views must equal fresh evaluation).

Run all ten fixture scenarios through the protocol and show the protocol path matches the direct engine path; also the integrating subscription equivalence test across object, cover and log scopes (vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.20). Exclusive files: `packages/authority/test/protocol-runner/*.ts`, `test/protocol-scenarios.test.ts`. Reuses vtt-75c.13's test helpers (`documentFromSetup`, `runScenario` with `onStep`, `RunReport`, value comparison) by import and never edits `test/runner/`; if a needed helper is not exported from its module, export it with a one-line change.

`runScenarioOverProtocol(scenario, {onStep?}): Promise<RunReport>`: `documentFromSetup` → `TableHost.inMemory(store, {dice: new ScriptedDiceSource(scenario.dice)})` (vtt-5su.4, vtt-75c.15) → `startServer` on port 0 (vtt-5su.10) → a `ProtocolClient` (vtt-5su.7, `kind: "test"`, Node's `WebSocket`). Steps: `set` and `override` → `transact [set_value]` (the M2 runner's scenario errors are decided from the GM view's `kind` per PROTOCOL.md §7.2: `set` is a scenario error when `kind` is `"formula"` (structural cells such as `position` included), `override` is a scenario error unless `kind` is `"formula"`, `clear_override` unless `overridden` is true; a `"structural"` or `"literal"` cell takes `set`); `clear_override` → `clear_override`; `move` → `move`; `spawn` → `spawn` with `as`, and `owned` bindings taken from the result's `copies`; `undo` → `undo {type:"latest"}`; `bind` → the contents of `in` (or `list_objects` with the tag filter) compared on GM views by FORMULAS §4 equality; a step's actor → `actor` param (characters as `{type:"character", id}`, GM by default); `base_revision` = the client's revision. Expectations: `cell`, `cell_error`, `override` from the GM view; `exists` from `missing`; `container`, `contents`, `placement` from structural cells; `object_visible` = present in `get_objects` with that viewer; `cell_visible` = the cell is present in that viewer's view (`cells` has the key), whatever its value, so a readable cell holding a redacted ref is visible (FIXTURES §7); `log_groups` from `log`; `log_includes` from `explain_group` (GM `EffectView`s); `replay` from `document`: vtt-75c.16's `replay` of the groups over the setup snapshot, compared with `storedStateEqual`; `rejected` from `status: "rejected"` mapped through `toFixtureReason` (vtt-75c.4). Truncation and skipped expectations exactly as the M2 runner (invoke stops the run; `action` expectations skipped and counted). After setup and after every executed step, `onStep({step, snapshot})` is called with the `document` result's snapshot (step -1 for setup).

Per-step comparison: the test runs each scenario twice, through vtt-75c.13's `runScenario(s, {onStep})` and through `runScenarioOverProtocol(s, {onStep})`, collects both snapshot sequences, and compares them pairwise.

Subscription equivalence (`test/subscription-equivalence.test.ts`, also exclusive to this bead): through `startServer` on port 0 and `ProtocolClient` mirrors (vtt-5su.7), seeded random sequences of 200 commits over a 60-object table (writes, formula sets, overrides set and cleared, moves between boards and containers, spawns, creates and removes inside containers, reorders, tag and shape edits, template and character flag changes including Aldric's own `is_character`, `set_actions`, board add, rename and remove, literal and override refs to objects and boards that are later removed, `visible_to` changes on containers, opaque zone toggles and moves including erroneous `opaque`, face flips, per-cell visibility, undo), for the GM and Aldric and for `board`, `objects` (subtree), `all` and `log` scopes: after every commit each mirror (objects, covers, log-window groups) equals the result of a fresh `subscribe` with the same params at that revision.

Done when: `protocol-scenarios.test.ts` produces for all ten scenarios the same `RunReport` table as vtt-75c.13's `scenarios.test.ts`; for every scenario the two `onStep` sequences have the same length and each pair of snapshots is equal by `storedStateEqual` with identity included; a test shows that `set` on a structural cell holding a formula (`position`) is a scenario error in both runners and `override` on it is accepted in both; a test shows `cell_visible` true for a cell whose value is `{type:"redacted"}` in the viewer's view; `subscription-equivalence.test.ts` passes for at least 5 seeds (seeds printed on failure); a self-test shows a wrong expected value fails with the scenario title, step index and expectation named; the server and client are closed after each scenario; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: `invoke`, `action` expectations and action rejections (M5); round-trip mode over the protocol (the direct runner covers it); new scenarios; fixture format changes; edits to `test/runner/` beyond one-line exports.

Depends on: vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.4, vtt-5su.7, vtt-5su.8, vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.16, vtt-5su.20, vtt-75c.13.

title: Authority: scenario runner (M2 subset)
description:
Implements: FIXTURES.md §1–§8 and §11 (as amended by vtt-75c.2, including `cell_visibility` mapping, the `replay` expectation and the rejection protocol for M2 step types); DESIGN.md §7; the runner contract in planning bead vtt-75c.1 comment 1.

Add @vtt/fixtures as a workspace devDependency of @vtt/authority and the runner in packages/authority/test/runner/ (test code, so M5 can extend it without a public API): setup.ts (`documentFromSetup`), steps.ts, expect.ts, run.ts (`runScenario`), plus packages/authority/test/scenarios.test.ts.

- `documentFromSetup(setup)`: boards; objects with `is_template`, `is_zone`, `tag`, `shape`, `contents`; `placement` → `board` plus a `position` cell (literal list or formula); `cells` → `Cell`s; `cell_visibility` → the object's `cell_visibility` metadata verbatim (any cell name, including structural and absent cells); `is_character` true for ids in `setup.characters`; actions copied as source; `revision 0`, `next_seq 0`. Fixture values are the schema values (the FIXTURES §2 encoding is the schema encoding), so conversion is the identity, checked with `isValue`.
- Steps: `set` (`writeValue`; a scenario error if the cell holds a formula), `override` (`writeValue`; scenario error unless a formula), `clear_override` (scenario error without an override), `move`, `spawn` (initial cells passed as cell content: literals through `writeValue`, formulas through `setFormula`; binds `as` and each `owned` key through the returned copy map), `undo` (`{type:"latest"}`), `bind` (tag, `where` by vtt-o9i.6's `equals` on `table.value`, `in`; zero or several matches is a scenario error; no group, no dice). `actor` maps to `Actor` (`gm` or `character`). Bindings resolve everywhere ids are used. Acting on a removed object is a scenario error.
- Every step runs through `transactWithDice` (vtt-75c.15): a `Rejected` is a refusal handled by the rejection protocol below; a `ScenarioError` (bad script, bad binding, set on a formula cell, …) propagates and fails the scenario as a scenario error, never as a refusal.
- Rejection protocol for the steps above: a refused primitive appends no group; a `rejected` expectation predicts it with the reason mapped by `toFixtureReason` (vtt-75c.4); an unpredicted refusal or a predicted one that does not happen fails.
- Expectations: `cell` (structural equality on tagged values: numbers exact, roll results all fields, lists elementwise), `cell_error`, `override`, `exists`, `container`, `placement` (evaluated position), `contents`, `cell_visible`, `object_visible`, `log_groups`, `log_includes` (`write` matches a `cell` effect whose resolved `after` value equals; `roll` matches a `cause: "roll"` effect; negative indices from the end), `replay` (vtt-75c.16's `replay` of the retained groups from the setup snapshot, compared with `toSnapshot()` by `storedStateEqual` (revision excluded), and the dice source's `remaining()` is unchanged). Any other expectation on a removed object is a scenario error.
- Truncation: the runner stops before the first `invoke` step and reports the scenario as partial. Expectations of type `action` are skipped and counted (they need M5's `when` handling). Leftover dice entries are a scenario error only for complete runs. `invoke`, `action`, and `when_*`/`step_error` rejections are M5's to add.
- Round-trip mode (`runScenario(s, { roundTrip: true })`): after setup and after every step, `serializeTable` → `parseTable` (vtt-75c.11) and continue on the loaded table, asserting snapshot and log equality at each hop. This is how "Save. Close. Reopen; everything, including the log, the undo… is there" is tested without a format change.
- `RunReport`: `{ title, complete: boolean, stepsRun, stepsTotal, skipped: Record<type, count> }`.
- Observation hook (for vtt-5su.12's per-step comparison): `runScenario(s, { onStep?: (report: StepReport) => void })` with `StepReport = { step: number; snapshot: Snapshot }`, called once after setup (`step: -1`) and once after every executed step (refused steps included, skipped `invoke` steps not), with `table.store.toSnapshot()` at that point (in round-trip mode, of the reloaded table). The hook only observes: its return value is ignored, it receives a copy, and nothing else in the run depends on it. Exported from `run.ts` with `StepReport`.

scenarios.test.ts runs every scenario in both modes and asserts the report against this table, so M5 must update it when it adds `invoke`:

| Scenario file | Status at M2 end | Steps run | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| hit-points.json | complete | 5/5 | none |
| difficult-terrain.json | complete | 4/4 | none |
| re-hiding-room.json | complete | 6/6 | none |
| goblin-hit.json | partial | 4/6 | none |
| attack-card.json | partial | 2/7 | 6 `action` |
| fireball.json | partial | 2/12 | 2 `action` |
| die-with-modifier.json | partial | 1/7 | none |
| dice-tray.json | partial | 0/10 (setup expectations only) | none |
| drawing-a-card.json | partial | 0/4 (setup expectations only) | 1 `action` |
| shuffling.json | partial | 0/2 (setup expectations only) | 1 `action` |

Done when: scenarios.test.ts passes with exactly the table above in both modes (every non-skipped expectation in the run prefix holds, including the `replay` entries vtt-75c.2 added to the three complete scenarios and to fireball.json step 1); runner self-tests in test/runner/*.test.ts show that a wrong `cell` value, a missing predicted rejection, an unpredicted rejection, an unknown binding, a `set` on a formula cell, and a leftover dice entry in a complete run each fail with a message naming the scenario, step index and expectation; a test feeds a `ScriptedDiceSource` through `rollInto` to show script consumption and `remaining()`; a synthetic spawn whose initial cell is a formula (`modifier = owner.attack_bonus`) stores the formula and its value recomputes after commit (and again after `attack_bonus` changes); a scripted-dice mismatch inside a step is reported as a scenario error, not a rejection; `onStep` is called `stepsRun + 1` times with steps -1, 0, 1, … and its snapshots equal the table's state after each step (checked on hit-points.json), and a hook that mutates its argument does not change the run; a synthetic setup with `cell_visibility` entries on `contents` and `tag` (no such cells) converts, survives a round-trip hop unchanged, and is honoured by `cell_visible`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); `invoke` steps, `action` expectations, `when_false`, `when_error`, `step_error` rejections (M5); new scenarios; changes to the fixture format beyond vtt-75c.2.

Depends on: vtt-75c.5, vtt-75c.16, vtt-75c.14, vtt-75c.12, vtt-75c.15, vtt-75c.11, vtt-75c.17, vtt-75c.2.

(b) undo and bind do not go through transactWithDice: undo owns its own transaction and bind opens none; neither consumes dice. The bead's 'every step' wording means every dice-consuming transactional step.

title: Formula: §10 acceptance suite
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 (every formula and `when` of every fixture, evaluated), §2.2, §4, §5, §6, §7 as exercised by them; docs/FIXTURES.md §9 (the states each scenario passes through).

The runner (vtt-o9i.10) stops at the first `invoke`, `spawn`, `undo`, or `bind` step, so most §10 formulas are never evaluated in the states those steps reach. This bead proves every §10 formula against those states by building them directly in a `MemoryHost` (vtt-o9i.15): literal roll results written with `set` in place of rolls, spawned objects added to the setup in place of `spawn`, and placements reached with `MemoryHost.move`, so spatial functions run on real geometry. One test file per fixture, test/acceptance/<scenario>.test.ts, each test quoting the scenario expectation it mirrors (scenario title + step index) and loading the formula sources from the scenario file itself (not retyped), so a fixture edit cannot silently diverge.

Cases (values are the scenarios' expected values):

- Hit points: 27, 22, and 17 after `damage_taken` 10.
- Die with a modifier: loose die `total` 0 → 14 after `value` = roll 14; Aldric's die `modifier` 5, `total` 5 → 16 (roll 11) → 17 after `attack_bonus` 6; goblin's die 4 → 13 (roll 9).
- Goblin HIT: `hit` false with nothing on the goblin and with a die beside it (footprints not overlapping), true with die1 (`value` roll 15, `total = value + modifier`) on top with higher `z`, false with a die whose total is 12, false with only a non-`d20` object on top.
- Dice tray: zone variant (dice moved into the tray's rect) and cup variant (the `contents` cell); sums 0, a die, two dice, a non-die ignored; a die leaving the cup changes the cup's sum.
- Difficult terrain: the scenario's `speed` formula (`zones_containing(this)` composed with `where` and the library) gives 30 / 15 / 30 as the token moves into and out of the difficult zone (composed query + library assertion moved here from vtt-o9i.8).
- Attack card: `bonus` 5; `total` 5 before the roll, 17 after roll 12; `hit` false before the roll (target empty: short-circuit), true with goblin `ac` 13; the three `when` guards via `engine.evaluate` at each state (Roll enabled only with target set and no roll; Roll damage only when hit and no dmg; Apply only when hit, dmg set, not applied).
- Fireball: `dc` = caster's `spell_dc`; `targets` = `[goblin1, goblin2]` with the zone moved to [10,10] on the map; `rows` from the card's `contents` cell; per row `card` = ref to the card, `save_bonus`, `passed`, and `damage_dealt` = 14 (a number) on a pass and the roll result itself (`{expr:"8d6", dice:[3,5,2,6,4,1,6,1], dropped:[], total:28}`) on a fail; the drift step (`dex_save` -5 flips a pass to a fail); Apply all's guard false with one `save_roll` empty, true with both.
- Drawing a card: `len(deck.contents) > 0` true, true, false as the deck empties; `first(deck.contents)` is the top card.
- Re-hiding a room: the room's `visible_to` formula (`contents(this).where(tag has "pc")` composed with `len` and `if`) gives viewers `["gm"]` / `["all"]` / `["gm"]` as the PC moves in and out (composed assertion moved here from vtt-o9i.8).
- Shuffling: no formula; the file asserts that and nothing else.

Done when: every case above passes; every formula and `when` source in every scenario is evaluated by at least one test (a meta-test collects the sources from the scenario files and fails listing any not exercised). `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); executing action steps, rolling, spawning, visibility, log (vtt-75c.13, M5); changing scenarios or the fixture format.

Depends on: vtt-o9i.15, vtt-o9i.7, vtt-o9i.8, vtt-o9i.16, vtt-o9i.12.

Add a root tsconfig.json extending the base that includes root *.ts config files, and make the root typecheck script run tsc --noEmit -p . before pnpm -r --parallel typecheck. title: Authority: ActionContext.read clones the change summary on every read
description:
Implements: DESIGN §7 (transactions), performance only.

ActionContext.read (packages/authority/src/engine/action-context.ts, vtt-75c.15) calls tx.changes() on each read to apply the 'changed in this transaction' rule, and Transaction.changes() structuredClones the ChangeSummary. Cost grows with reads × summary size. Fine for M2; worth fixing before large actions in M3+.

Done when: reading a cell through ActionContext does not copy the summary (e.g. a cheap change counter on the transaction, or a read-only summary view), with the existing action-context tests unchanged and a test that a 1000-read action over a transaction with 1000 changed cells stays well under a second.

Out of scope: any semantic change to the rules in ActionContext.

Depends on: nothing.

title: Docs: FIXTURES.md §9 Fireball example uses a stale 8d6 roll
description:
Implements: docs/FIXTURES.md §9 (Fireball example only).

docs/FIXTURES.md §9 (around lines 246, 404, 611) shows the Fireball 8d6 roll as dice [3,5,2,6,4,1,6,1] total 28, giving damage_dealt 14 on a pass and roll(28) on a fail. The committed fixture packages/fixtures/scenarios/fireball.json scripts [3,5,2,6,4,1,5,1] total 27 (13 on a pass, 27 on a fail; Apply results goblin1 13, goblin2 30), and its description text agrees with 27. The engine agrees with the fixture (vtt-o9i.11 acceptance suite). Found while implementing vtt-o9i.11.

Done when: the §9 example values match fireball.json (dice, total, pass/fail damage_dealt, Apply results). No fixture or code change.

Out of scope: any change to fireball.json or the acceptance tests.

Depends on: nothing.

title: Protocol: persistent txn_id deduplication
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (idempotent retries).

The txn_id cache (vtt-5su.5) is in memory and lost on authority restart, so a retry across a restart may double-apply. Persist recent txn_ids (e.g. on each group) so a repeat after restart returns the original result.

Done when: commit with txn_id, restart the authority from the file, resend: no new group, the original result is returned.

Out of scope: cross-table dedup.

Depends on: vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.4. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q8.)

title: Authority: automatic log compaction policy
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence (log compaction allowed; the log panel shows what is retained).

v1 never compacts automatically (vtt-5su.4). Decide and implement a policy (e.g. keep the last N groups or groups newer than D days, at save time) on top of compactLog (vtt-75c.11), recorded in the decision log.

Done when: the policy is configurable on TableHost, runs at save, keeps absolute indices and barrier rules, and a test shows undo below the kept range is nothing_to_undo and changes_since reports truncated.

Out of scope: in-memory checkpoints.

Depends on: vtt-5su.4. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q24.)

title: Protocol: read-set preconditions on transact
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 (writes rejected on conflict), docs/PROTOCOL.md §6.

The stale-write rule (vtt-5su.5) refuses only when an intervening group touched a key the transaction writes. Add an optional expect: [{object, cell}] read set to transact, refused stale_write when an intervening group touched any of those keys, so a write computed from a value that changed meanwhile is caught.

Done when: a transact with base_revision r writing B and expecting A is refused after an intervening write to A and commits otherwise; PROTOCOL.md and the MCP transact tool schema document the field.

Out of scope: automatic rebase.

Depends on: vtt-5su.5. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q7 c.)

title: Protocol: cell-level deltas in commit events
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §8 (subscriptions, commit events), FORMULAS.md §7 (propagation).

Commit events currently upsert whole object views (vtt-5su.9). Send cell-level patches ({object, cells: {name: CellView | null}}) instead, as an additive protocol extension negotiated in hello, to cut bandwidth for large sheets.

Done when: the vtt-5su.9 equivalence property test passes with patch deltas; ViewMirror (vtt-5su.7) applies patches; a protocol version or capability flag keeps old clients working.

Out of scope: changing which cells are recomputed.

Depends on: vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.7. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q10.)

title: Fixtures: quote prose in card and Fireball scenario notes
description: attack-card.json, drawing-a-card.json, shuffling.json and fireball.json have expectation notes without a prose quotation or rule citation; the cells scenarios (vtt-1me.9) were brought up to that standard after review. Audit and bring the other four to the same standard without changing expected values. Out of scope: any value change.

title: Vitest empty-project reporter misbehaves in watch mode
description: From Codex review of vtt-1me.3. In watch mode, deleting a package's last test file does not trigger onTestRunEnd, and after a later rerun detects it, restoring the test leaves process.exitCode at 1. Fix: track per-project state and clear exitCode on recovery, or skip the guard in watch mode. Root vitest.config.ts.

title: Polish
description: Standing epic. Review findings and ideas that are real but not needed for the current milestone. Triage into a milestone when it matters.

title: Protocol: chunked initial subscription snapshots
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §8 (subscriptions), §10 (limits); DESIGN.md §7 (scale: tables of a few thousand objects).

In v1 server-to-client messages have no size limit: an initial `subscribe` result for an `all` or large `board` scope is one message, and the slow-consumer threshold `max_buffered_bytes` is 64 MiB (vtt-5su.2, vtt-5su.10). For much larger tables (see vtt-y1w.4, very large map performance) deliver initial views in bounded chunks with a revision-consistent completion boundary: the subscription is pinned to the revision of its first chunk, commits after it are queued and delivered after the final chunk, and a reconnect restarts the snapshot without looping on the same failure.

Done when: a subscription over a table whose initial view exceeds a configured chunk size arrives in several chunks over the real transport, the mirror equals a fresh subscribe at the completion revision, commits made during delivery are applied after completion, and an additive protocol extension (PROTOCOL.md §12) keeps v1 clients working.

Out of scope: cell-level deltas (vtt-qf5.4); tiling of map images (vtt-y1w.4).

Depends on: vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.7, vtt-5su.19. (Followup from M3 plan review r1, finding 21.)

title: Protocol: persistent command deduplication across authority restarts
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §6 (deduplication, client retries, `uncertain`), DESIGN.md §7 (persistence).

In v1 the (`client.instance`, `txn_id`) deduplication store is in memory (vtt-5su.5), so it is lost when the authority restarts; clients then report a lost write as `uncertain` instead of retrying, and a retained-entry miss is `retry_unknown` (vtt-5su.19, vtt-5su.5). Persist recent deduplication entries (client instance, txn id, fingerprint, result) with the table, e.g. on each group or in a bounded section of the file, so a retry after a restart returns the original result and clients may retry across a `session` change.

Done when: commit with a `txn_id`, save, restart the authority from the file, resend from the same client instance: no new group and the original result is returned; a resend with a different fingerprint is rejected `invalid`; PROTOCOL.md §6 and the client retry rule are updated (retry across sessions allowed for persisted entries); the file format change is a migration step and recorded in the decision log.

Out of scope: cross-table deduplication; deduplication of `undo`.

Depends on: vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.4, vtt-5su.19. (Followup from M3 plan review r1, finding 12. Supersedes the earlier Polish bead vtt-qf5.7, which predates the client-instance scoping.)

title: MCP: Streamable HTTP transport
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 (bring your own agent).

v1 serves MCP over stdio from vtt-mcp (vtt-5su.11). Add an in-process Streamable HTTP endpoint for agent hosts that prefer HTTP.

Done when: an MCP client over HTTP lists the same tools as over stdio and passes the same tool tests.

Out of scope: auth beyond the local token.

Depends on: vtt-5su.11. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q1 a.)

title: Protocol: multiplayer rights over actor and viewer
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §8.2 (participants mapped to characters, rights model), §4.4.

In v1 every connection has GM authority and viewer is a view-as selector, not a security boundary (vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.6). Multiplayer must bind a connection to participants, enforce viewer server-side, and gate writes by the rights model; commit-event group headers and labels must then be filtered per viewer.

Done when: to be planned with multiplayer.

Out of scope: v1.

Depends on: vtt-5su.10. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q4, Q9, Q15.)

title: Authority: remote access over TLS
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform, §8.2 (multiplayer needs a server authority).

v1 binds 127.0.0.1 with a per-start token (vtt-5su.10). Serving remote clients needs TLS, a non-loopback bind option and stronger auth.

Done when: to be planned with multiplayer.

Out of scope: v1.

Depends on: vtt-5su.10. (Followup from the M3 plan, Q4.)

title: Drop the fixtures Node typing shim
description: packages/fixtures/src/node.d.ts hand-declares node:fs/promises, node:path and import.meta.dirname because the package typecheck does not see the root @types/node. Make packages that use Node built-ins see @types/node properly (types in their tsconfig or a devDependency) and delete the shim.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Observed in vtt-75c.12: test files outside @vtt/formula cannot import packages/formula/test/support/memory-host.ts because its type-only import of @vtt/fixtures pulls fixtures' Node-only src/index.ts into the importing package's typecheck (TS2591 node:fs/promises). vtt-75c.12 restated literalCandidates in its own test instead. Fixing the shim should also let authority tests reuse formula's test hosts.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: vtt-75c.17 added '/// <reference types="node" />' in packages/authority/src/persist/io.ts (root @types/node 26.6.6), which makes Node globals visible across the whole authority type program. The fixtures node.d.ts comment saying the workspace has no @types/node is now stale. Resolve both when fixing the shim: give the packages that need Node an explicit types setting and drop the ad hoc reference.
